body:
MAGA is shocked we're competitive. A Black farmer from rural Louisiana isn't supposed to threaten their Senate seat. But here we are. | | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138207655/643425739/1254121610?refcode=260831_jamie_magashock&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjAwMzEiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMDQ0MmUzZGQtZDBhNC1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5YThkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=XL5dVwwiq5_1PJRPIXCdr0mv2ofrgnVs0FGrhN347Z0=)

Let me be honest with you about something.
I'm not supposed to be in this race.
The grandson of a sharecropper? Not supposed to be a viable Senate candidate in Louisiana.
A Black farmer from rural Tensas Parish? Not supposed to compete statewide in the Deep South.
Someone without billionaire backers or a Rolodex full of Washington insiders? Not supposed to have a shot at flipping a Senate seat.
But here we are.
**And MAGA is absolutely shocked.**
They thought Louisiana was locked up. They thought they could focus on defending seats in swing states while the South stayed safely red. They thought a race like ours — a real populist challenge to their grip on power — wasn't possible here.
They were wrong.
Look at what's happening: Democrats flipping Trump districts across the South. MAGA candidates tearing each other apart in primaries. Republican retirements at levels not seen since the Great Depression. Trump's approval cratering over his failed Iran war.
This is a once-in-a-lifetime opening. The kind of moment that doesn't come around often in Louisiana politics.
**_And I believe — deep in my bones — that this is the campaign to meet this moment._**
Not because I'm the most polished politician. Not because I've been planning a Senate run my whole career. But because I understand what working Louisianans need because I've lived their struggles.

| | | |
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138207709/643431396/-642992695?amount=25&refcode=260830em_sjj_ai-eom3&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84OTMxMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1NzJmMTU4ZC1kMmE0LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=6xaAm0nYnwxC_O2H9lk7YywSzBSDrpBViwZGa2qGX_w=)
---
Let’s talk about AI. I’m a millennial, which means I grew up in that strange in-between tech era — an analog early childhood, but high school and college in the world of iPhones. I remember the early internet emerging: sitting down in front of our family computer, the screechy sound dial-up made, the cringeworthy AIM screen names and away messages (_if you know, you know_). _We watched technology go from a novelty to something that shaped nearly every part of how we live and work in a few decades._ And now, as one of the youngest members of Congress, I find myself at the center of what is the most consequential shift of our lifetimes: the rise of artificial intelligence. AI is one of my top priorities, and like I’ve heard from many of you, it often keeps me up at night. **I think about it like this: we’re all standing on a beach watching a huge wave roll in, and we can’t tell yet if it's something we can surf, or a tsunami that will take us out. I believe it's the government's job to make sure AI is a wave we can surf — and right now, it’s not doing enough.** Put simply, Congress has just been too slow on this. clean_body: | | | | = Let’s talk about AI. I’m a millennial, which means I grew up in that strange in-between tech era — an analog early childhood, but high school and college in the world of iPhones. I remember the early internet emerging: sitting down in front of our family computer, the screechy sound dial-up made, the cringeworthy AIM screen names and away messages (if you know, you know). We watched technology go from a novelty to something that shaped nearly every part of how we live and work in a few decades. And now, as one of the youngest members of Congress, I find myself at the center of what is the most consequential shift of our lifetimes: the rise of artificial intelligence. AI is one of my top priorities, and like I’ve heard from many of you, it often keeps me up at night. I think about it like this: we’re all standing on a beach watching a huge wave roll in, and we can’t tell yet if it's something we can surf, or a tsunami that will take us out. I believe it's the government's job to make sure AI is a wave we can surf — and right now, it’s not doing enough. Put simply, Congress has just been too slow on this. I've spent the last year introducing AI legislation to try and change that, including the AI Talent Act , the Sectoral AI Governance Act , and most recently the AI Tax and Work Protection Act. That last bill levies a tax on AI companies based on their usage and revenue. The goal is simple: if AI companies eliminate jobs, they’ll pay more in taxes — and that money will go directly to creating new jobs in the public interest to replace the ones lost. I'm proud to be leading this fight, and when Democrats win back the House majority in November, we’ll be able to move critical AI legislation forward to begin protecting Americans amid this huge transition. But all of that depends on whether we flip the House in nine short weeks. Peter, let
me tell you what I did NOT spend time doing today.

I didn't spend any time on the phone with corporate PACs.

I didn't spend time asking a single corporate lobbyist for a campaign
check in exchange for a favor later on in the Senate.

That’s because I've never taken a dime of corporate PAC money, and I never
will.

Unlike Mike Rogers — who's too busy courting MAGA billionaires from his
Florida mansion — I spend the majority of my time focused on Michiganders.

I’m talking with folks on the street and in union halls and classrooms,
asking them about what's actually going on in their lives. That's the
whole job as far as I'm concerned.

But my finance team would beg to differ. 😂

The truth is, we still have a massive fundraising budget gap to close.

We need resources to get ads on the air, fund our travel across the state,
and reach the undecided voters who'll decide this race.

name: Roy Cooper
subject: This email is exactly six sentences
body:
Out of respect for your time, I’ll keep it quick
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1189&source=&t=1&akid=3052%2E124072%2ERd0zAJ) | | | |
---
Peter,
With only one day left until our end-of-month deadline and a $2 million goal to reach, [**_I’m personally asking you to make your first donation to my campaign_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1189&amount=5&t=8&akid=3052%2E124072%2ERd0zAJ) to help us close the gap in time.
Back when I ran for Governor in 2016, all the numbers and polls seemed to be in our favor – but I ended up winning by just 0.22% of the vote, and President Trump carried North Carolina in the presidential election.
Ten years later, I’m up against his handpicked candidate in the race experts say will decide Senate control, and the predictions appear to be on our side once again.
**But now, GOP dark money is flooding our race – and a brand-new poll shows me statistically tied with my MAGA opponent. Peter, if I learned anything from 2016, it’s that we cannot take this race for granted.**
[**_Before tomorrow’s critical deadline, will you chip in $5 for the first time to make sure we have the resources to fight back, flip North Carolina blue and take back the Senate?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1189&amount=5&t=9&akid=3052%2E124072%2ERd0zAJ)

Roy Cooper

Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

[**_Donate today to help win this seat and flip the Senate blue._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1189&source=&t=3&akid=3052%2E124072%2ERd0zAJ)

Hi Peter,

and I can completely understand why. Everyday people are sick and tired of

streamer than fight Donald Trump’s worsening corruption and fascism.

make it even bigger.

they need to win.

In solidarity,

Alexandra Rojas
Executive Director

clean_body: Republicans defied the electoral process. | = Peter, The Republican Party just picked its new nominee through a backroom deal that shut voters out completely. No election. No community input. Just insiders picking their own replacement behind closed doors. Western North Carolina does not need another round of insider politics and the same broken agenda dressed up with a new name. We need leadership that takes Hurricane Helene recovery seriously, respects working families, and actually knows what it means to show up for people when life gets hard. Jennifer Balkcom is an insider who has already taken tens of thousands of dollars from corporate interests in Raleigh. In the legislature, she voted her party line nearly every time – and in fact, one of the only times she broke ranks was to vote against Medicaid expansion, trying to keep hundreds of thousands of our neighbors from more affordable health insurance. The name may change — but the priorities do not. More of the same failed politics, more of the same distractions, and still no real plan to deliver for families trying to recover from Hurricane Helene, just whatever the party bosses say to do. Truth be told, this race is about more than one candidate or one party decision. It is about whether our region keeps getting pushed aside or whether we build something better together. I’ve spent my life around people who understand work, responsibility, and looking out for your neighbors. That’s the kind of leadership I’m trying to bring to Congress.= = Jamie Ager Democrat for US Congress | If you would like to receive fewer emails, we understand. to sign up for only the most important updates, or you can . I want to share a bit about my personal life that you may not know yet. ** ** I was raised by social justice warriors.** ** My dad marched for civil rights in Selma, Alabama, where he heard Martin Luther King Jr. preach. ** ** My mom, born and raised in the Philippines, spent years fighting for the restoration of democracy in her home country. ** ** They had me while living and working in the Philippines as social justice missionaries. I was born when a dictator was rising to power and martial law was imminent. ** ** It was critical to both of my parents that I grow up in a country with democracy, freedom, rule of law, and human and civil rights — and sadly it became clear to them that wasn’t the case in the Philippines. So they brought my family here, to California, when I was just two months old.
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138208190/643456629/2110272206?amount=25&refcode=260830em_rb_sjw&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmNmFlYWM5OC1kOWE0LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=L300FUwlU4b5l3TFPOJ08O4bq-gWxROk8N7-lOEvOiQ=)
---
A short while later, my parents began working with the United Farm Workers of America — fighting for workers’ rights, fair pay, and shade and water breaks alongside Dolores Huerta and Philip Vera Cruz. ** ** I would never have guessed as a young kid that I would grow up to serve as the Attorney General of California — but as long as I can remember, I’ve known that I wanted to fight for those most vulnerable to have a fair shot at the California Dream.** ** That’s why I do this work. I know, without a doubt, that the California Dream is alive and well because I’m living mine — and I’m committed to using every bit of platform and power I have to lift people up and fight for justice for all. ** ** I’m on the ballot for re-election this November, and I want nothing more than to continue this fight. ** ****California needs an Attorney General who will stand up to those who abuse their power** — whether it’s corrupt politicians, corporate polluters, extremist groups trying to roll back our rights, or powerful interests that exploit workers, cheat consumers, and put profits ahead of people. ** ** **[We have an important end-of-month deadline tomorrow at midnight, and every single dollar we raise before then will make an impact on what we can do — in my re-election campaign, and in our movement to secure justice and accountability for all. clean_body: | | | | = I want to share a bit about my personal life that you may not know yet. I was raised by social justice warriors. My dad marched for civil rights in Selma, Alabama, where he heard Martin Luther King Jr. preach. My mom, born and raised in the Philippines, spent years fighting for the restoration of democracy in her home country. They had me while living and working in the Philippines as social justice missionaries. I was born when a dictator was rising to power and martial law was imminent. It was critical to both of my parents that I grow up in a country with democracy, freedom, rule of law, and human and civil rights — and sadly it became clear to them that wasn’t the case in the Philippines. So they brought my family here, to California, when I was just two months old. = A short while later, my parents began working with the United Farm Workers of America — fighting for workers’ rights, fair pay, and shade and water breaks alongside Dolores Huerta and Philip Vera Cruz. I would never have guessed as a young kid that I would grow up to serve as the Attorney General of California — but as long as I can remember, I’ve known that I wanted to fight for those most vulnerable to have a fair shot at the California Dream. That’s why I do this work. I know, without a doubt, that the California Dream is alive and well because I’m living mine — and I’m committed to using every bit of platform and power I have to lift people up and fight for justice for all. I’m on the ballot for re-election this November, and I want nothing more than to continue this fight. Federal agents took Marvin Godoy Calderon - a janitor with a legal work permit - off a San Francisco street in broad daylight.

They choked Iryna Gorb at SFO. They arrested a 5-year-old, Liam Conejo Ramos, to lure his mother out of her home; he's now in a detention center 1,300 miles away.

In Minneapolis, they shot and killed Renee Good and Alex Pretti in broad daylight and they are refusing to investigate.

Almost none of these people can sue because a loophole in federal law has made ICE agents essentially immune from the Constitution.

Yesterday, the California Legislature passed my No Kings Act to end that loophole.

**My No Kings Act lets Californians take ICE, Border Patrol, and other federal agents to court when they violate our constitutional rights - and we made it retroactive to March 2025, so people whose rights have already been violated get a path to justice too. It's the first bill in the country to do this.**

**It is now on Governor Newsom's desk but he only has until September 30 to act. If he signs it, it takes effect immediately.**

But Republican outside groups have already spent or reserved more than $10 million in advertising here, and this race is a pure toss-up.** Waiting while they fill the airwaves attacking me isn’t much of a strategy. **[So I’m asking: Will you chip in $5, $10, or whatever you can today to help us cover this ad buy and keep our message on the air?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138208361/643460907/-995582223?refcode=260830-greenlight-rs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTkyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4MDBhYzg3Yy1kYmE0LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=PjuxrkykeNBSKOR4m3MVg9le9sycnX1MW3cxVVwmGw4=)**

Here’s why we made the call now. TV time gets harder—and more expensive—to secure as Election Day gets closer. If we wait until every dollar is sitting in the bank, the best opportunities to reach voters could already be gone. Meanwhile, national Republicans know exactly how important this seat is. Donald Trump carried our district twice. Speaker Mike Johnson came here personally to raise money for my opponent. And Republican groups with hundreds of millions of dollars to spend have made it clear that Southwest Washington is one of their top targets. **They can afford to wait us out. We can’t afford to let them.** I don’t take corporate PAC money. We don't have billionaires waiting in the wings to write whatever check we need. What we have is a campaign that has won this district twice because thousands of people decided it was worth putting some skin in the game. So I made a bet that if we committed the money now, this grassroots team would help us close the gap. **I’m counting on that bet paying off.** [**Please make a contribution today to help us pay for these ads, stay competitive on TV, and win one of the closest House races in America.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138208363/643460909/-995582223?refcode=260830-greenlight-rs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTkyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4MDBhYzg3Yy1kYmE0LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=PjuxrkykeNBSKOR4m3MVg9le9sycnX1MW3cxVVwmGw4=) Thank you,Marie Gluesenkamp Perez

If y'all think the 2026 Midterms are still ways off, I've got news for ya: [They're coming at us like a runaway shopping cart in a Walmart parking lot.](https://trk.email.tim-burchett._cmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTM1JmV4X3RpZD0yMDI2MDgzMV9ZTi0yVy4xMTAxMTdfdDIwMDQ1OTYtNDEyNSZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249MjAyNjA4MzFfWU4tMlcuMTEwMTE3X3QyMDA0NTk2LTQxMjUifQ/f7d72sFTZIQ1I0vnbhjYrA)
And while we're talking, the professional politicians are already doing what they always do: dialing up wealthy donors, lobbyists, and special-interest groups to fill up the campaign coffers.
That's their business.
Mine is representing East Tennessee and making life uncomfortable for the folks who think your tax dollars belong to them.
But my team keeps reminding me that if we want to keep fighting, we've got to keep the lights on.
Unfortunately, they're right.
So we've set a goal to get ahead of our August End-of-Month Deadline: [$10,000 raised from grassroots conservatives by TONIGHT.](https://trk.email.tim-burchett._cmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTM1JmV4X3RpZD0yMDI2MDgzMV9ZTi0yVy4xMTAxMTdfdDIwMDQ1OTYtNDEyNSZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249MjAyNjA4MzFfWU4tMlcuMTEwMTE3X3QyMDA0NTk2LTQxMjUifQ/CFu29zw8g_qqVDJqgSbgbQ)
Now, $10,000 may not sound like much to the Washington crowd.
But if we raise it one dollar at a time from thousands of conservatives across this country, it'll send a message louder than any consultant's PowerPoint presentation.

## Iran Strikes US Bases after Hormuz Raid
Six months of [war with Iran](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL3OnTAQRJ_GdL5a24D5Chdp6G7alMjActnEP8heQMnTR-QV0o000mjO-fGe3p4Cpc93H9HxlqeEdw3IjOWJVHyqXOgX1phzipSwVD9p0L2EQRo1-YXpwqn1zeo2RI2mQafsMCgL1nTN7uYNYDHaQjd_KQCjYMb2y9t1AYDerg25Zw8GoxRAZ-C1gFeLB-s726KftWgBV-JcXj8zJd5xC7_zheW15NgEtzMfVZhvQo9Cj_d9v5a5PhxPL_QY6EJ5HqtnrEKPD5O8fZFnlVzOeMjKxRPLvMk9l3j-kb2MOfFeZcoS0yopyUqfnYUem-LW46YQqPZWtPCJnsK_I_yf_i6n_wYAAP__IwmHbQ) flared back to life Sunday. U.S. forces struck two Iranian rocket launchers, and Iran answered with ballistic missiles aimed at American air bases in Jordan. The launchers sat on [Larak Island](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1u6zAMhZ_G3hToz5Y1aLhLtty1o8HIdMxWtgKJSdA-faH2EbrxA4GD8523y3wBSnTc_sOOgdc8H_iqCZmxtJMKHJULfWDdcz52OrBUmLXUo5CTMGqGyPTE2UK_hBVRo-kxKDdNyklnhn4LYBb0MK3OwxC988YrjVpFbxtdsafQ8uRklJJyMPIUJagI0sHgLMJVd1biQpzL6T3TwRuu6TM_sZxi3vsUNuZ77cy_Tp87fYZ7U2ivBoUpJuz0uZmIygWIxZbL_vgSv2LicRDjIioDYxXjVfppgdEZiEaNCvQ4ItrBLwOuq7V9Ccv9RSlRHV1n5W0HSj9F-I_7PYP-DgAA___jYYXb), where Revolutionary Guard forces were preparing to fire new sea mines into the Strait of Hormuz just one week after the U.S. finished clearing it. Iran's retaliation targeted two U.S. air bases in Jordan. The Jordanian military said it intercepted all eight missiles that crossed into its airspace, and no damage was reported. [Watch the report here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuhDAQBNCvMd2h9drYXOEiDd2lTYn28HK3icEnY0Hy9xH5hXQjjfSkmY_beCNJsj7eaeFQ5zyufGyJa-VyRim0brXIF29LzusiK5eNRgR0F-gvRo80Vdl5tNTEMDMjm4aD9n2vPXjTNc9w913UrK8Rr2Rm766ebX933KM1LnpqJJwe9EZrgM5AOwHpicBT5y3THZUFjlJzaT-zrPXJc_rJO5d2ykuTwrPW16bMm8JB4XAcRzvn73PH2SscdomcFQ7OgjWm885pjU0J8XVISrI5ryw8FpL0B9Z__rAH_A0AAP__B4FxGA). The exchange was the first fighting in a month, and it lands as Washington presses its economic campaign. The Treasury secretary plans new bank sanctions this week, telling the media, _"This is going to be financial violence if we have to."_

**A Note from Cole, CEO of _The Flyover_** Dear Reader, This week, _The Flyover_ crossed six million total readers.

Before anything else, thank you. A milestone like this belongs to the people who open our email every morning--that's you. But the number isn't the point. The point is what six million of you showed up _for_ , and what you have walked away _from_. You know what's on the other channel. Anchors telling you what to think before they've told you what happened. So-called "straight news" pages that read like opinion pages. The legacy media had one job: reporting the news, and somewhere along the way, they decided their real job was converting you to their ideology. The slant isn't an accident, and it isn't decided in front of you. It happens in rooms you'll never see. Every so often, the door cracks open: last fall, an investigation revealed that a legacy media outlet had spliced a presidential speech into something it never was. Two top executives resigned. That's one leak from one room. The decisions that never leak? Those just become the evening news. We run on the opposite principle: the truth survives the light. The facts arrive the way we found them. We don't bend them toward a conclusion, and we don't decide what you're allowed to make of them. That's your job. **We report what happened, not what to think about it.**

U.S. forces struck two Iranian rocket launchers, and Iran answered with ballistic missiles aimed at American air bases in Jordan. | | | | | | Monday, August 31, 2026 ---|--- Good Morning! On this day in 1955, General Motors engineer William Cobb unveiled the world's first solar-powered car at an auto show in Chicago. The "Sunmobile" ran on 12 tiny solar cells and measured just 15 inches long. . Three years ago, Warner Bros. locked a finished Looney Tunes for a tax break. Fans howled, a tiny distributor swooped in, and this weekend Wile E. Coyote finally got his day at the box office. See how sweet the revenge was in Finance. Today's sponsor is built around a refreshingly practical idea: getting healthier shouldn't require completely changing your life. Simple focuses on small, sustainable habits you can incorporate wherever you are--without restrictive diets, complicated routines, or spending hours at the gym. | Iran Strikes US Bases after Hormuz Raid Six months of flared back to life Sunday. U.S. forces struck two Iranian rocket launchers, and Iran answered with ballistic missiles aimed at American air bases in Jordan. The launchers sat on , where Revolutionary Guard forces were preparing to fire new sea mines into the Strait of Hormuz just one week after the U.S. finished clearing it. Iran's retaliation targeted two U.S. air bases in Jordan. The Jordanian military said it intercepted all eight missiles that crossed into its airspace, and no damage was reported. . The exchange was the first fighting in a month, and it lands as Washington presses its economic campaign. The Treasury secretary plans new bank sanctions this week, telling the media, "This is going to be financial violence if we have to." Venezuelan Oil to Refill US Reserve President Trump said Sunday that oil from the new Venezuela deal will refill the , which sits near a 44-year low. He called the crude a "Gift from Venezuela to the People of the United States." Details keep emerging two days later. Venezuela's acting President Delcy Rodriguez says the agreement will , and the U.S. is reportedly taking a 35% stake in a Venezuelan oil mogul's private venture. Sen. Ted Cruz praised the deal in an interview Sunday but said in Venezuela must follow "no later than midway through next year," adding the administration is "working rapidly" toward them. For drivers, relief may take a while. Gas averaged Sunday, up from $3.19 a year ago, and Venezuela's battered oil fields need major investment before production can rise. NASA Telescope Launches on Planet Hunt NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy from Florida's Kennedy Space Center. It now begins a three-month, million-mile journey to its deep-space post, with first images expected early next year. The telescope was built around a donated mirror originally made for a spy satellite, and its wide-angle images are so vast that displaying one in full would take half a million 4K TVs. . Cleveland reached a population of 914,808 in 1950. The latest [U.S. Census Bureau estimate puts the city at approximately 363,608 residents](https://substack.com/redirect/eb24ca03-e78a-4efc-a2fa-5a92eb8fb841?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
The city has lost about 60 percent of its population since its peak, but it still occupies roughly the same 78 square miles.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8577a6a5-f637-48be-989f-7dbe34282357?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[Cleveland 1970](https://substack.com/redirect/42c12a59-ca1f-414c-bb13-f66f938f5592?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s
One thing I have watched over the years, living and growing up around Cleveland, is suburban sprawl. It is the movement from the city to the suburbs, then to the outer suburbs, and then even farther out.
I paid attention to it because I was part of it.
I grew up in [Slavic Village](https://substack.com/redirect/dd0e3d32-3e66-4f53-88ea-61e8c4945cdf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Then I moved to Bedford. From there, I moved farther out to Geauga County and Solon, with some stints in Twinsburg and Streetsboro. My brother now lives in Macedonia. My mom lives in Streetsboro. My dad lives in Solon.
I have watched people hop from the inner city to the inner suburbs, from the inner suburbs to the outer suburbs, and then farther and farther away.
There are understandable reasons people do it. They want newer homes, newer schools, newer roads, more space, less crime, or a fresh start. Sometimes an older house costs $150,000 or $200,000 but still needs another $100,000 worth of work. It might need new electrical wiring, grounded outlets, plumbing, HVAC, windows, roofing, asbestos removal, lead remediation, or a completely updated interior.
Then a builder offers a new house farther out for $280,000 or $300,000. Stretch the budget a little more and everything is new.
I understand that decision.
But every time we move farther out, we do not pick up the roads, sewers, water lines, schools, streetlights, police stations and fire stations we left behind.
Those remain.
We build another set farther away.
That has led me to a hypothesis I have been working through: **the modern American suburban development pattern may not be financially sustainable over the long term.**
This is a hypothesis and a thought experiment. I am not claiming that every suburb is bankrupt or that nobody should own a single-family home. I am asking whether cities with relatively low population density can collect enough revenue to maintain all the infrastructure and services spread across their physical footprint.
The evidence suggests that the lower the density, the more infrastructure each taxpayer is being asked to support.
* * *
## More Northeast Ohio, but Not More Northeast Ohioans
Cleveland's population peaked in 1950 and since then the city has lost about 60 percent of its population, but it still occupies roughly the same 78 square miles.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7911168b-f4ad-4de9-96cc-ef5d481cdf98?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[Cleveland Population Decline](https://substack.com/redirect/6c7d585d-2216-41dc-a188-96fdfc8ba856?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The roads still need to be maintained. The sewers still need to work. The streetlights still need to stay on. Police, fire and emergency services still have to cover the city. Schools still have to be operated or replaced. Bridges still have to be repaired.
A water main does not become 60 percent cheaper because fewer people live above it. Actually, because of inflation that water main becomes more and more expensive.
The population did not simply disappear. Much of it moved.
The Cleveland Planning Commission found that developed property in Cuyahoga County [covered more than twice as much land in 2000 as it did in 1950, even though the county's population was nearly identical in those two years](https://substack.com/redirect/ecaa07ff-1ee3-42f0-aa75-27f0cbf9f2ca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
There were more individual households because families became smaller, but the general pattern is still clear. We spread roughly the same population across dramatically more land.
We built more roads, more subdivisions, more sewer lines, more schools, more commercial developments and more emergency-service territory without bringing a comparable number of new people into the region.
Regional planners have been warning about this for years. In 2013, [Vibrant NEO 2040](https://substack.com/redirect/a1e9cfd9-1fdb-4be1-8de7-2f603a2bcbe8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) modeled what could happen if Northeast Ohio continued with business as usual. It projected only **2.4 percent regional population growth from 2010 through 2040 while adding 92,500 acres of new development and abandoning 77,100 acres of existing property.**
That was a projection, not a final count of what has happened. But it described the pattern I have watched my entire life.
**If Cleveland loses 10,000 people and Streetsboro gains 10,000 people, Northeast Ohio did not gain 10,000 taxpayers.**
But the region may now have the streets those people left behind plus the new streets built for them. It may have the old sewer system plus new sewer extensions. It may have old school buildings plus new school buildings. Police and fire departments still have to cover the older communities while new departments and facilities cover the expanding outer suburbs.
That is the question underneath my hypothesis.
Are we actually growing, or are we spreading the same population across a larger and more expensive and costly system. **And ... do we need to rethink how we live in America?**
* * *
## Bedford as a Thought Experiment
I lived in Bedford for six years when I was young, so I am going to use Bedford as an example.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/cfdc97e6-c295-4222-8d58-d8395270639f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[Bedford, Ohio](https://substack.com/redirect/0a7dbaa2-0a81-401e-b5bc-e5f97a757c23?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Again, this is a thought experiment. I am not arguing that every financial problem in Bedford was caused by suburban sprawl.
Bedford had 17,552 residents in 1970. The Census Bureau now estimates approximately [12,723 residents](https://substack.com/redirect/5cb7c813-a35d-4236-8e19-6a266b0559ab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The city's current median household income is about $57,300. Which is down from over $70k average salary (adjusted for infltation) in the 1970's.
Bedford still has the streets, schools and public infrastructure of a community built during a different economic and demographic era. It has fewer people helping to support much of that infrastructure.
Glendale Primary School is a prime example of what an aging system can look like.
In 2026, a broken sewer pipe in an upstairs boys bathroom leaked into the school kitchen. The kitchen closed, meals were prepared elsewhere, and approximately 300 children ate in the gym. After the first pipe was repaired and the kitchen reopened, [a second leak from the girls bathroom forced it to close again](https://substack.com/redirect/a874293a-cd35-403c-9ae4-8e3809e3626a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
The building is nearly 100 years old.
The Bedford City School District passed a $161 million construction bond and is replacing several aging facilities, including building a new primary school, middle school and high school. The district's [facilities plan](https://substack.com/redirect/058e334c-90d6-4c02-a2ef-d8601d188881?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) calls for demolishing Glendale and other old buildings.
Passing that bond was probably necessary. Children cannot continue attending school under leaking sewer lines.
Bonds are not inherently bad, either. A school will be used for generations, so spreading the cost across generations can make financial sense.
But the bond is still debt, and somebody has to repay it.
The question is whether communities with declining populations, stagnant or declining wages and aging infrastructure can continue to meet these replacement costs without continually raising taxes, taking on more debt, or depending on money from outside the community.
Bedford is not alone.
Across NOACA's five-county region, the agency tracks approximately 3,300 centerline miles of major roads, 3,100 bridges and five transit agencies. NOACA estimated [accumulated maintenance costs from 2020 through 2024 at $380 million for roads, $240 million for bridges and $340 million for transit](https://substack.com/redirect/bb50294b-e107-4dc7-b297-474e093c26ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
That is approximately $960 million across only those three categories.
It does not include every local residential street, water line, sewer, stormwater system, school building, fire station, police department, sidewalk, park or streetlight.
The region already relies on outside funding to help maintain and improve this system. [NOACA receives approximately $51 million annually](https://substack.com/redirect/722d5d6b-e13b-44be-b35c-88bebdc65a78?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from the Federal Highway Administration, Federal Transit Administration and Ohio Department of Transportation to allocate to projects across its five counties.
That does not prove that every individual city is insolvent. State and federal governments normally help finance infrastructure.
It does show that the system is not maintained entirely through the taxes collected by each city from its own residents.
* * *
## Density Changes the Math
The basic math is not complicated.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b681a8bd-128c-4da1-b8e4-da0a0a47c507?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[Single Family Homes Macedonia, Ohio](https://substack.com/redirect/9f38d289-bdbf-4f4c-b26b-a2f5e8ca9b12?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Imagine a street that is 1,000 or 2,000 feet long. It has 60 detached houses and perhaps 120 people living on it.
That street needs pavement, snow removal, drainage, water, sewer, streetlights, police protection, fire protection and emergency medical coverage.
Now imagine that same street with duplexes, triplexes, apartments, townhouses, small businesses or mixed-use buildings. Instead of 120 people, it might have several hundred people living and working along the same stretch of infrastructure.
The city still has to maintain the road and pipes, but the cost is now spread across more households, more businesses and more economic activity.
A national analysis of compact development estimated that controlled growth could save [approximately $110 billion in road construction and $12.6 billion in water and sewer infrastructure](https://substack.com/redirect/b2551cd1-9c49-433e-bf76-37dd52b688af?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Fire protection provides another example. A [Charlotte case study summarized by the Environmental Protection Agency](https://substack.com/redirect/71863759-2da7-4c14-92ab-43063d9e49e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) found that a fire station in a connected, compact neighborhood could cover 4.5 times as many addresses as a station serving a sprawling neighborhood. The estimated annualized cost was $159 per person in the compact area compared with $740 in the lower-density area.
It is the same basic public service. Density allows the cost of the station, equipment and firefighters to be spread across more people.
Schools work somewhat differently because Ohio's school-funding system is complicated and school districts do not always follow municipal boundaries. But density still affects transportation.
[Ohio's school transportation formula uses both students and miles driven and defines density as riders per square mile](https://substack.com/redirect/3e6e1547-39bd-49fb-b832-88fd41f37554?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). A lower-density district may have to send buses farther to reach fewer children.
Police and emergency services face the same geographic problem. A department has to cover the entire physical area of a community regardless of whether that area contains 5,000 residents or 50,000 residents.
The farther people spread out, the longer the network becomes.
There are more roads, longer bus routes, more sewer extensions and a larger area for police, fire and ambulances to cover.
Then, in 20, 30 or 50 years, all of it begins to age.
* * *
## Why People Keep Moving Outward
This is not just a government-budget problem. Housing plays a major role.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fe0fb640-46c2-4b8b-8fbd-ccf0fb512b86?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
East Cleveland, Ohio
Older communities often have older housing stock. The houses may have been built in the 1940s, 1950s, 1960s or 1970s. Some have outdated floor plans, old wiring, old plumbing, aging HVAC systems, lead paint, asbestos or foundations that need serious work.
People look at a house selling for $150,000 or $200,000 and then realize it needs another $50,000 or $100,000 in repairs.
Farther out, a builder is selling a new home for $280,000 or $300,000.
Why buy the old house?
The newer house has a modern floor plan, grounded electrical outlets, a new roof, new plumbing, a new furnace and fewer immediate repair expenses. The roads and surrounding infrastructure are also newer.
The individual buyer is making a rational decision based on what is best for that household.
But the regional effect is that people continue moving outward. The older home and older infrastructure remain behind. New homes and new infrastructure are added farther away.
Eventually the new community will face the same problem. The roads will age. The schools will age. The sewer lines will age. The houses will need major repairs.
Then another development may be built even farther out.
* * *
## Ohio's Other Cities Show the Same Pattern
The **Cleveland** numbers become even more revealing when we compare them with Ohio's other major metropolitan areas. Special thank you to [Jasson Farrier](https://open.substack.com/users/308847628-jasson-farrier?utm_source=mentions) for collecting the data. **[Check his You Tube here.](https://substack.com/redirect/2b0c7349-d072-4acf-afae-b7797d6cc098?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
According to an analysis of the [U.S. Census Bureau's American Community Survey housing data](https://substack.com/redirect/c11f1a4a-d39e-4e05-afdf-cd8b02485158?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the Cleveland metropolitan area added 17,544 housing units from 2011 through 2024. That sounds like growth until you look at where the housing was built.
**Cuyahoga** **County** lost 6,876 housing units while every surrounding county gained. Geauga added 1,262. Lake added 5,509. Medina added 7,547. Lorain added 10,102.
In other words, the region added housing, but the county containing its largest city lost housing while development continued moving outward.
The five ZIP codes losing the most single-family homes were all in Cleveland or East Cleveland. The five gaining the most were in North Ridgeville, Medina, Avon, Painesville and Avon Lake.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fd916f76-0edb-45c3-8371-e3e6613e7d9a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[https://www.communitysolutions.com/resources/population-changes-clevelands-inner-ring-suburbs](https://substack.com/redirect/2209cb96-5d5b-4743-8c17-40b54233e3ed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
This data does not literally track a family moving from one particular Cleveland house into one particular Medina County subdivision. Housing units can disappear through demolition, conversion or abandonment. But it shows where the region is investing and where its housing stock is disappearing.
We are building outward while allowing parts of the existing core to hollow out.
**Cincinnati** shows a similar pattern. Hamilton County, which contains Cincinnati, added 3,241 housing units between 2011 and 2024. Warren County added 16,046, nearly five times as many. Clermont County added 8,154 and Butler County added 7,614.
**Cincinnati 's** core is not collapsing like Cleveland's, but the direction is similar. The city ZIP codes losing the most single-family homes are inside Cincinnati, while places such as Mason, West Chester and Loveland are adding thousands.
**Akron** shows how this can happen even when countywide numbers look healthy. Summit County added 3,107 housing units and neighboring Portage County added 4,098. Neither county shrank.
But inside **Akron** , ZIP code 44304 **lost** 59 percent of its single-family homes between 2011 and 2024. Several older Akron ZIP codes lost hundreds of homes while Aurora, Stow, Twinsburg and Streetsboro added housing.
That is not simply city versus suburb. Parts of Akron are gaining while other neighborhoods a few miles away are collapsing. It is the same underlying problem happening at a smaller geographic level. New housing and investment flow toward the communities and neighborhoods with newer roads, newer schools and newer infrastructure while older areas are left with fewer homes and **taxpayers** supporting systems built for more people.
The real question is whether Northeast Ohio can keep building new versions of itself farther outward while expecting every older community left behind to maintain infrastructure designed for a larger population and tax base.
At some point, we are not creating growth. We are setting ourselves up for high taxes and financial strain.
* * *
## We Have to Rethink How Cities Are Built
If the hypothesis is correct, then continually raising property taxes, income taxes, sales taxes and fees will not fix the underlying problem.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ff0fa0b8-ab01-4eb4-b900-dd198888a4bc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The problem is not only how much revenue the city collects. It is how much infrastructure that revenue must support.
Cities that have lost population need to consider whether their zoning laws are preventing them from adding enough residents and businesses to use the infrastructure they already have.
Large areas are still zoned around an idealized 1950s lifestyle: **one detached house, one yard, one garage, one car in the driveway and several children.**
But household demographics have changed. More people live alone. People marry later. Some couples do not have children. People are having children in their late thirties and forties. Not everybody needs or wants the same kind of house.
Cities should allow more duplexes, triplexes, multifamily buildings, mixed-use buildings and, where appropriate, tiny homes. Property owners should have more freedom to add households to existing lots.
Instead of receiving revenue from one household on a lot, a city could receive revenue connected to two, three or four households using the same street, sewer and water line.
That does not mean every neighborhood has to become a collection of high-rises. It means cities should stop assuming that detached single-family housing must be the only legal option across enormous portions of their land.
**Transportation also has to be part of the discussion.**
Cleveland has too many damn parking lots, too much land dedicated to roads and parking, and not enough useful public transportation. RTA should have been redesigned a long time ago.
Cities should be willing to reconsider parking requirements, buses, rail, bike infrastructure, ride sharing and other ways people can move without requiring every person to own and park a car everywhere they go.
We may also need to ask difficult questions about city limits and the number of separate governments managing shared infrastructure. Should boundaries expand? Should services be shared differently? Should some areas operate separately?
I do not know the answer. I am asking whether the current arrangement makes sense when roads, sewers, jobs and transportation systems cross all these municipal boundaries anyway.
* * *
## Is the American Suburban Lifestyle Sustainable?
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/72943e0e-429b-4442-9002-e85f680937e7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Pulte Home
This is the real question. 👆🏽
Can cities maintain roads, bridges, sewers, schools, police departments, fire departments and public transportation when their populations are spread across low-density neighborhoods and their tax bases are not growing fast enough to cover replacement costs?
Can Northeast Ohio continue moving from Cleveland to Bedford and Maple Heights, then to Solon, Northfield and Macedonia, and then to Canal Fulton and beyond, while still expecting every community left behind to maintain what was already built?
Or do we have to rethink the way we live?
Again, this is a hypothesis. But the population numbers, land-development patterns and infrastructure costs suggest that it is a question worth taking seriously.
The American ideal of a detached house on a large lot, with a driveway, a garage and all the infrastructure needed to support it, may not be financially sustainable everywhere forever.
If we want older cities to survive, we may need higher-density housing, walkable neighborhoods, better public transportation and zoning laws that allow more people and economic activity to use the infrastructure we already have.

Yes, cities might have to just say do what you want on your land and build housing and business.
We cannot keep moving farther out, building another version of the same city and expecting the old one to maintain itself with fewer people.
At some point, the replacement bill arrives.

name: Roy Cooper
subject: A difficult decision
body:
This race is too consequential to sit out. The stakes are too high.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1191&source=&t=1&akid=3080%2E124072%2EoNXlwm) | | | |
---
Peter, deciding to run for this U.S. Senate seat wasn’t easy.
I had planned on serving North Carolina from here at home. That’s why I was so humbled when North Carolinians twice elected me to be their Governor.
**But this Senate race is too consequential to sit out. The stakes are simply too high.**
I entered this race to fight for people like you, who’ve put your trust in me – and I have full faith that together, we can win. But tonight, we’re facing the biggest test yet of our grassroots movement’s strength.
After 11:59 p.m., our end-of-month deadline will come to a close. [**_So with time running out to reach our ambitious $2 million goal, I’m personally asking you to help out by making your first $5 donation, right now._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1191&amount=5&t=8&akid=3080%2E124072%2EoNXlwm)
| | [DONATE](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1191&amount=5&t=9&akid=3080%2E124072%2EoNXlwm)
---
I’m running because our nation cannot afford two more years of unchecked Republican power in Washington. The attacks on health care, on democratic values and even on Americans – **they have to stop.**
Our leaders should be focusing on strengthening our communities by investing in public schools, securing health care access and prioritizing hardworking folks over the wealthiest few. That’s what I strove to do in North Carolina – and by the end of my time in office, we added thousands of jobs by expanding the clean energy economy, gave public school teachers statewide a much-needed raise, expanded Medicaid and more.
**This is the work I’m ready to continue as the next Senator from North Carolina. That means we have to flip this seat from red to blue for the first time in a generation and take back the Senate for the people who elect us, which is easier said than done.**
I’ve never lost a race, but this one will be the most competitive of my career. It’s the best pick-up opportunity for Democrats this cycle, and our ability to flip the Senate hinges on us succeeding. That’s why far-right groups are already spending nearly $100 million so far to attack me – and experts expect this to be the most expensive Senate race ever, so they will spare no expense to help President Trump’s handpicked candidate buy his way to victory.
So if they see us missing goals like the one we set for tonight, they _will_ use this as an opportunity to strike. They _will_ flood the airwaves with millions more in attack ads to smear me, knowing that their investments are working as intended, because we _will not_ have enough funds to fight back.
[**_Chipping in $5, $25 or whatever amount is right for you before the end of the day won’t just help us close the gap in time; it’ll prove to everyone that momentum is on our side. So if you’re with us, Peter, please make it clear by making a donation right away._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1191&amount=5&t=10&akid=3080%2E124072%2EoNXlwm)
_If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_ | | | [DONATE $5](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14275?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1191&amount=5&t=11&akid=3080%2E124072%2EoNXlwm)
---

---

Roy Cooper

We are grateful for your support and no further action is required at this time._
| |

[](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1191&t=2&akid=3080%2E124072%2EoNXlwm)
Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

[**_Donate today to help win this seat and flip the Senate blue._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1191&source=&t=3&akid=3080%2E124072%2EoNXlwm)

## San Antonio Storm Outages Dropping
CPS Energy had [fewer than 20,000 customers](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkTuO4zAQBU9DZW3wJ1EOFGyibDbdUGiRbZkYmhTItmXffqG5wsQFFF7h_ftavjCmmLe_-KCJ37eyZDpaImaqC73ZP_eEH6r-jnWjwPTGxmXRUg8gRzBqQc_xRYvFLkyrDFfV0aTcOCpnlbp29ymsZK9kSRJqLSkY1-OJx3GQkvq-i9Opk6NRSknVu4uWg7Vr72jwg-ndKKykELnUC9_pZ8ItfcqL6sWXR5emO_PehPkj9Cz0fBzH5Zty608q9IyVo08k9HymCT2n4jEJPfu9AWWq2wfKk3GjBqGWHVZK5QAtvwEbNC71AT4R5ucOMUPDDJi55FjAl8wxP-m0amfAyAHlahT4FS1Y5yysV92DJONvTuqr0qGrU9iPmFJsgxNWbg-M6SeEf3vAa9L_AwAA___jE5mk) without power Sunday after a Friday night storm knocked out power to more than 100,000 homes at its peak. Outages were down another 6,000 by mid-Sunday. Interim CPS President Frank Almaraz said restoration will stretch into the start of the week. Pedernales Electric Cooperative sent 50 lineworkers, nearly doubling the utility's capacity. Crews repaired more than 100 downed wires overnight on Saturday, [the city said](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0E_uoyAYxvHT4A4D-Ae6YDHp1F2bps1klobCq5KgGHhH6-0n7RV-F3ieT75_r_3V-OCX8WZm0PgeYr_AngMgQurhjfbfGswByU4mjeAQ3iZj7AUTLWWKVrw3Fv0GfW0Kp1_MnXgBmkuluKw5PxWTHtrGSCkH5pRQjWO2bZgApgQX7tWceOH1Z46pinPOeCNLwdq6fjUSWttWjVSkZuA8xlTiBF_CEI64QSptnIugJ8Q1k-oXER0R3b7vZTblGDciut8-gcWYDiK6G-yZPiCAyZCJ6M4eD3q-P-llgTQe9J7i5h3QP6szCDQu9IkxzfQB9nN20MswxIS5SNqtuw_B51aSmo2z8eFLwZ8m3LT4HwAA___dJoeO). Poles and transformer crews won't be able to reach some areas until debris is cleared. Mayor Gina Ortiz Jones confirmed [one storm death](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOtCAUhZ8GOw2gAlNQ_I3d_O2W5oJXJUEwcHecefvNTPYNtj_n5Dvf132-Q4ghbf_hQEvPNc8JrxqRCMuMT_LfZ4QXFr9D2XAhfEKlPEsuVctN24sZPIUHzgM0i3V8uYkGrdDGCD0IcWt268AZrpU0Tq_rKNWojeNoxOgUGDf6Jtj3HDe9EIKLUXeSq2Fwo0blVT9qwwaOS6BcOtrxg7DGV35g6Xw-mmh3orOy_h-TE5PTdV3d8aqQIFFOIb9DTE7vX0xOMXuITE5QKPiITE5LyVcKaWsrpPa301bK5WgXBNpbKQd-M0Z15342xS7nFWIMVWk28O2AED8Y9Fd9Dyt_AgAA__9y-IYu): a 46-year-old woman, believed to be homeless, was swept into San Pedro Creek north of downtown Friday and found dead Saturday. Police are also investigating a man's body pulled from Woodlawn Lake on Sunday. Six resilience hubs will remain open until noon today, and the Food Bank has planned three distribution sites. SAISD is running a normal schedule. Some [119 traffic signals](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDvO2zAQhE8jdWtwaVqPgkUad3_alMKaWkoEKFIg1w_dPpCRG6T9MBh8M39-ph8KMaTlN21s5ePzlPhdI4twmfgj7rlHOri4lcrCs_CHquRJK92BGuCKEzkJL54MtbN9qHnEli32w4C9QRzb1Xrfe63NA_3DD6Pz6HnEEceh68abN9gGe9ap4YqICm_9RavOmMet585111s_NEbxHCSXi6z8VfDxyC8uF5e3NtpVZK_N9Vej742-nwNMpURJcgr5zPyjjb7H7Cg2-u6CHOD2Cpy4LAdIhiW8GFABbfDcZxIGqiBrflZKc4XCG4UE73AigT2_uQB54QJVctlqW-y8v0OMoXZ9Y9SyUYhfQ_nfZ19W_w0AAP__9hiRxQ) were dark on Sunday morning. ## Ex-TCU Player Charged over Punch
Former TCU safety Jacob Fields turned himself in Sunday on a [charge of aggravated assault](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD1ygzAUhE8DHczTD5IoVKShc9qUjJAeRhlhMdKLjW-fsXOE9Du7-31fl_niYoq366fb0dK55vmGj5qQCMuMJ_mfI7knFr-5csVAeLpKeebAVQemE2x2nuIdZ-naYBcII2vRMm0M05Kxsd3sigBhYQKMwaDM4mBdBjF4oTgfjRzbaF91YARjDNigew5KymXQqLwSgzaNBAyRculpw_eFNT3zHUvv894muxEdtREfDZ8aPtUjF6r90205vwINn1yh6BPWhk_fzuelWyOmULs_qtrheSQXbxi6NZcdS8f0oECCNP1Ge2qLDccjphSr0o2E6-5iem_Tf53dLf8NAAD__4ZsggE) causing serious bodily injury. Agent Philip Miller [told ESPN](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOrCAYRp8GOwwgglNQ3IZubrulQfhVNigG_hmdt9_MZN9g6y85Od_5uo93F1Pcl_9uA4PXnMcdzpoAEcoIF_rHkdwLil9dWSAgXK5iHgUTirKBdnx0HuMTRumaYCYWbrwBw_UwcC05vzWrEcDVBMx3alBT0FLP3Ktu7r0MrAclm2jeODZ0nHPGe90KpqSceg3Kq67XA5EMQsRcWlzhozCnV35CaX3emmRWxKOS7h8Rlgh7nmcL9djfIxHW55RgATrnjJNLiQhbMZcXEXYkwsZAhJU3rYXmkggLF0X_oJV-O58nOkdIodLf-9R9WIEej92vFMFtm0NoignHGVOKVWki2bK5mD5u-NemTyN-AgAA__-gfYxk) that Fields was held at the Tarrant County Jail in Fort Worth and expected to post bond yesterday. The charge stems from an Aug. 13 locker room altercation in which Fields allegedly punched Horned Frogs receiver Dozie Ezukanma. TCU general manager Ryan Dorchester [called campus police](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2y4yAQBODToAwXoB-kgGATZW_TDVUDjGR2R0YFY8nv9lv2FV7e1fV1__laviBRemy_YUfHrzUvD7wqITOWBV8cngfBN5Zwh7JhZHxB5bwYZQapRtnqBQKnE5cOmui8ipNu0Gk7jtp2Wk_N3Wm0k1IwgV81xnaINngN_QTjqkbft01y7zo1tlprpXt7M2roOt9bHMLQ9nYUncKYOJcb3_FDWOk7n1huIe8NuTvzUUX7S5hZmPm6rlvwtR65cH0nhJlDJsIN5ZozeyASZn7vFGZec9mxSA5PWeVfCNnLNSHFKmHbCpzAGCXUCk9iSTn8wyJLzrsEYiwBOOWHMHNTXDyuRJTqYEWnth0SfXj801tPZ_4HAAD__8kYkRA) the next day, and the school dismissed Fields on Aug. 18. In a since-deleted Instagram video, Ezukanma said he was "sucker punched" and knocked unconscious when his head hit the floor. Miller has [called much of what has circulated online](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OtCAUQJ8GOyaAKFhQfA3dfO2W5irXkQ2KgTs_vv1mZh9h65OcnJyv63iFmOJ--w8bOnotedzxWRMSYRnxRfP9SHBimVcoNwyEL6iURyVUz4XlrRxhpvjAUUMT3CTCIBt00lgrjZZyaFZnemmhRd0aPXQGQtBGGsCAwfY6DFMT3VsnbCulFLIzFyV6rafOYD_3bWcs0wJDpFwutOInYUlnfmC5zHlrkluJjsraf0x5pvx-HrnSGzHl32amvLBM-VYw5euRC1WmfIh1i7Vi4DTfeYUF6eTfMOeJLxFTqBxKwUoYeN451Ar3RPz3A1O-KS4cz5hSrL1hWtw2iOnTQ3_9-HDqJwAA__8NF4hA) "false or purely speculative." Fields will have no further comment, Miller said. The case also cost a reporter access to the program. TCU pulled the _Fort Worth Star-Telegram_ beat writer's credentials [over his coverage](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO6yAURL8Gd7YAY4MLite4y2u3tK7hYrMiwYKbOPn7VaL9g-1GGml05nxdlgvEFG_bf7iipWfIyw3PmpAIy4JPcvcjwQuL26Fs6AmfUCkvksux5abtxQKO4gMXBY23K_eTaNAKbYzQSoip2e24glGggludnIT2gwrcBTDDakLPUTXRvue46YUQXAy6k3xUah00jm7sB22Y4ugj5dLRjh-EkF75gaVz-dokuxMdlfX_mJyZnM_z7Nxe8u3dMjnXIxeqTM4up4QbMjlDoejSO5G7t9_g8tqGiMnX9vdoC7XCPVErpeKT0WN37EdTrD_OmFKso2aKb1eI6cNAf3X3sPInAAD__yDQhRw), saying it "endangered a student-athlete." Fields was Conference USA's Co-Defensive Player of the Year last season at Louisiana Tech.
## Texans Pay $615K in Lifetime Taxes
A new [Visual Capitalist map](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGuozAQRb8GOiPbgG0KF9vQvW23RIM9hJFMQPYEyN-vkl94_dU9R-ffz_QDlOj5-Asber6XfXriVRIyY57w5vA6ErwxhxXyAyPjDYX3SUtthHSiVRMEphOnDuroZxkHVaNX1jllO6WGevVqUMPgWgxBBmXn2YI1cZkx6qWPxrma_OdOulYpJVVvGy1N1829RRNM21tXdRIj8Z4bXvGrsKT3fmJuwr7Vya_MR6naP5UeKz1e19WcVF6QAhzEkKjwZ1jpcYPjwCgSLci0oWC4sQh6Cjwxv8VLFFEYGCs91tnH46KUqBhbdfKxAaUvj3_b6fT6fwAAAP__ugJ_qQ) puts the estimated lifetime tax bill for a single Texas filer at $615,932, landing the state near the middle of the national pack even though Texas levies no individual income tax. The figures come [from Self Financial](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGO6yAQgOHT4M4WgzE4BcVr3OW1W6IJDDESMRGejZ3brzZX2At8-vV_Xf0Vc8nb_T8-yPGZqt_o2AsxU_N0cvh-FnxTCyu2O0WmE3euXkllejn3I3gMnF_kNXbR3WS8QEcO7DyD1QCXbnXBWlRmHs0YTdIECDGmGAhxMtGk1GX3y8l5BAAJkx2UNFrfJksmmHGys9CSYubaBl7pk5DKu76oDaE-uuJW5ucuxn9CLUItx3EMO5U05C0IteQtVaGWkhP1NfWMp1BL11x8HrmUvBsrtLw_MJePxn-98HLqJwAA__9DmHJE), with estimates as of June 2026. They combine federal and state income taxes with sales, property, and vehicle taxes over a 45-year working life, assuming homeownership at 40 and five vehicles owned in a lifetime. New Jersey tops the ranking at $1.36 million, followed by Massachusetts at nearly $1.30 million and Connecticut at $1.25 million. New Hampshire and New York round out a top five dominated by the Northeast. Florida is the lowest at $508,980, followed by South Dakota, Arkansas, and Oklahoma, all under $527,000. Texas sits roughly $107,000 above Florida and far below Pennsylvania's $835,067. Washington, also with no state income tax, still ranks 16th at $816,217 per lifetime.

**A Note from Cole, CEO of _The Flyover_** Dear Reader, This week, _The Flyover's_ editions, including _The Texas Flyover_ , passed six million readers combined. Before anything else, thank you. A milestone like this belongs to the people who open our email every morning--that's you. But the number isn't the point. The point is what six million of you showed up _for_ , and what you have walked away _from_. You know what's on the other channel. You know . . . Americans really don't like data centers.
Opposition to having a data center built near you has surged to 75%, with 60% of Americans strongly [opposed](https://substack.com/redirect/803e3117-bf54-4c71-8a53-aa5b4ab217e9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Nearly half of Americans think that data centers generally are bad for the country. Concern about having one built near you is higher than it would be with a nuclear power plant.
This has been building for a while. I was on a panel in Michigan and was asked about the public sentiment. I responded, "Well, to the average American, the value proposition is, 'we're going to build something near you that will consume power and water, and might be noisy and an environmental problem, in service of a technology that might take your kid's job. And what you'll get in return is . . . unclear.' So it's little wonder that Americans aren't responding positively."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6882d94d-2d39-4cae-a8b3-23bd5660ceef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The political tide is turning. Despite the above, officeholders in both parties were reluctant to criticize the data centers because they are critical to the development and economics of AI and often brought with them an infrastructure buildout and tax revenue. Josh Shapiro, Governor of Pennsylvania, is a notable and typical example, who lauded the centers. Now, he's imposing [state regulations and limitations](https://substack.com/redirect/d166461e-74ea-496a-aa01-5a2d97658567?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
The early adopters of the anti-center backlash were the Bernie populist types, who sensed both a need and an opening. But now, even Republicans like Gov. Greg Abbott in Texas are pushing for a pause, as they are getting an earful about them everywhere they go. This is an issue that is close to 80-20 and is transcending party lines.
Big Tech got another black eye last week, as Meta settled a multi-state [lawsuit](https://substack.com/redirect/b5b792df-fc05-4011-9b4f-4442066afe0a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) alleging that its products harmed the mental health of children for $18 billion. It agreed to implement a set of features for minors, including a two-hour daily time limit, a mode where the kids can't use it between midnight and 6 am, and limits on notifications during school hours. While Meta didn't admit fault, the settlement sends a clear message that the tide is turning against them too. $18 billion isn't that big a deal to a $1.5 trillion company - about 1% of their value - but more lawsuits and restrictions are on the way. Meta is quickly becoming a reviled company to millions of families; I'm sure the upcoming sequel to "The Social Network" won't help.
Also last week, Bill Gates came out and said that society is totally unprepared for the impact of AI economically and socially. He [wrote](https://substack.com/redirect/6a59c022-4ce7-4e4b-816d-7458e5fdad39?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), "the silence is deafening" and can't believe that more isn't being done to guard against the downsides of effects like job displacement.
Thanks Bill.
So what happens now? Multiple data center projects are being delayed or scuttled. I don't see the public changing its mind on this one. The AI industry has a lot of bridge building to do but it's not actually built for a charm offensive. Meanwhile, Anthropic is gearing up for a trillion-dollar IPO as early as September and OpenAI is aiming for a similar public market debut in 2027. It's going to be harder for investors to remain enthusiastic about the AI bet if the compute timelines aren't feasible and protests are commonplace.
The AI industry has had its way since its launch. We're about to see how it handles adversity and how this influences the anti-incumbent midterms. The backlash is here.

name: Bill Gray
subject: These lessons aren't relics of the ancient world
body:
Is truth relative? That’s a question our culture answers very differently than it did even a generation ago.

| | | [](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckc2K2zAQgJ9Gvtnox7G1Bx-WOoFCd0ubQ-nJzGom9oAsCUlOX7-Epi-w1-8bvoGZX2_LG7DnsL7DThOXsmDEpW5UyFMpMRTIFGomz67E26KlHlppW6MWcJXvtPTQ4HTSyt5sQ5MarVXjaK1ptmmwoE_aWPMxKgcIL2ZAuPWoHH6MJ8CGp0dPWqOUlr0aO6vcC5I1UpKC3irRyyMhVOo4FEYqLsaUoufKrnQxr42ftlpTEeZV6IvQl0LuyNRt7H1B8NQRHkJfMAao9PBHSjHXtm7UsmdAYS6F1p1C_RKRhJmlkcq8S93rb-d5_j6fz1ehh6PuS4lHdo-RlGNJ5CqH9al2Qj52YWbagf0TOtgT8BqEmf-teuIYKoUqzGyklL_Prz-vy4-x_Xq9tv_P0eQJ0x_2nsswil6uj2rn4t7Uzz7pPum_AQAA__-aK6Kk)

| | Dear Fellow American, **Is truth relative?** That’s a question our culture answers very differently than it did even a generation ago. Many students today are taught that truth changes with the times—that each person has their OWN “truth,” and that yesterday’s convictions should give way to today’s feelings. **Hillsdale College is different. We pursue truth and defend liberty** and provide “sound learning” of the kind needed to preserve “the blessings of civil and religious liberty.” **[That’s one reason we created our free online course, “The Iliad.”](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckc2K2zAQgJ9Gvtnox7G1Bx-WOoFCd0ubQ-nJzGom9oAsCUlOX7-Epi-w1-8bvoGZX2_LG7DnsL7DThOXsmDEpW5UyFMpMRTIFGomz67E26KlHlppW6MWcJXvtPTQ4HTSyt5sQ5MarVXjaK1ptmmwoE_aWPMxKgcIL2ZAuPWoHH6MJ8CGp0dPWqOUlr0aO6vcC5I1UpKC3irRyyMhVOo4FEYqLsaUoufKrnQxr42ftlpTEeZV6IvQl0LuyNRt7H1B8NQRHkJfMAao9PBHSjHXtm7UsmdAYS6F1p1C_RKRhJmlkcq8S93rb-d5_j6fz1ehh6PuS4lHdo-RlGNJ5CqH9al2Qj52YWbagf0TOtgT8BqEmf-teuIYKoUqzGyklL_Prz-vy4-x_Xq9tv_P0eQJ0x_2nsswil6uj2rn4t7Uzz7pPum_AQAA__-aK6Kk)** For nearly **3,000 years** , readers have returned to Homer’s epic because **it tells the truth about the human condition:**
* It shows what pride can do to a great man.
* It shows why loyalty and friendship matter.
* It shows that courage demands sacrifice.

And it reminds us that there is **a moral order greater than ourselves.** **Those lessons aren’t relics of the ancient world. They’re as true today as they were when Homer first wrote them.** But too many young Americans never encounter books like _The Iliad_. Instead, they’re taught that truth is something we create for ourselves. **A free society cannot endure if it forgets the difference. That’s why I’m asking for your help today.** **Will you make a tax-deductible gift to help us raise $50,000 and introduce 100,000 Americans to these timeless lessons through Hillsdale’s free online course on _The Iliad_?** **[https://secure.hillsdale.edu/donate/support-the-iliad](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckc2K2zAQgJ9Gvtnox7G1Bx-WOoFCd0ubQ-nJzGom9oAsCUlOX7-Epi-w1-8bvoGZX2_LG7DnsL7DThOXsmDEpW5UyFMpMRTIFGomz67E26KlHlppW6MWcJXvtPTQ4HTSyt5sQ5MarVXjaK1ptmmwoE_aWPMxKgcIL2ZAuPWoHH6MJ8CGp0dPWqOUlr0aO6vcC5I1UpKC3irRyyMhVOo4FEYqLsaUoufKrnQxr42ftlpTEeZV6IvQl0LuyNRt7H1B8NQRHkJfMAao9PBHSjHXtm7UsmdAYS6F1p1C_RKRhJmlkcq8S93rb-d5_j6fz1ehh6PuS4lHdo-RlGNJ5CqH9al2Qj52YWbagf0TOtgT8BqEmf-teuIYKoUqzGyklL_Prz-vy4-x_Xq9tv_P0eQJ0x_2nsswil6uj2rn4t7Uzz7pPum_AQAA__-aK6Kk)** Your gift can help teach truth to more students and families. By giving **$25, $50, $100, or even $200 or more, you will make a difference.** Every one of Hillsdale’s free online courses is offered **without accepting a single penny of taxpayer funding—not even indirect funding through student grants and loans.** Our independence allows us to pursue truth without political pressure or government interference. **But it also means our work depends entirely on friends like you.** Thank you for helping Hillsdale preserve the truths that have sustained freedom for centuries. Warm regards, Bill Gray ’01
Vice President
Institutional Advancement
Hillsdale College

**About Senator John Hoeven** A North Dakota native born in Bismarck, John Hoeven has spent his career fighting for the people of the Peace Garden State. Before coming to Washington, he served **ten years as North Dakota's governor** — growing the economy, cutting taxes, and turning North Dakota into one of the nation's top energy producers.

Since being sworn in as U.S. Senator in 2011, Hoeven has brought that same commonsense approach to Washington. He's a leading voice for **American energy dominance** , a champion for North Dakota's farmers and ranchers, and a tireless defender of our military — including Minot Air Force Base, the nation's only dual-nuclear base.

\- August 31st, 2026 - **Bo French launches first TV Ad Buy ahead of November Election**
**MIDLAND** **-** Today, Bo French, Republican nominee for Texas Railroad Commissioner, launched his first major ad buy ahead of the November election. The advertisement focuses on the energy records of Bo French and his Democrat opponent, Jon Rosenthal. The advertisement is set to run multiple times per night across the Permian Basin until Election Day.
“Oil and gas are the foundation of the Texas economy, and the people need to know Jon Rosenthal is hell-bent on dismantling it,” said Bo French, Republican nominee for Texas Railroad Commissioner. “My opponent has campaigned for anti-energy radicals like Bernie Sanders, and as a legislator, introduced a multitude of bills attempting to derail the Texas Miracle.”
Bo French grew up in the Oil and Gas industry. His family has worked in the industry for more than 80 years, and his father was a wildcatter. Bo also has experience as an energy trader, giving him a depth of knowledge of the ins-and-outs of the Texas energy industry. “The choice in November is clear. James Talarico and Jon Rosenthal and the rest of the Democrat ticket are running on the most extreme liberal agenda Texas has ever seen. If Talarico and Rosenthal get their way, we’ll all have windmills in our backyards and Smart cars in our driveways. I am running to preserve the Texas way of life and preserve - not destroy - the Texas Miracle,” concluded French.
The TV ad was initially placed in the Midland TV market, with texting and streaming to follow.
To view the advertisement, visit the following [link to Bo’s X post](https://link.emails.bofrench.).
To learn more about Bo French’s campaign for Railroad Commissioner, visit [BoFrench.com](https://link.emails.bofrench.).
The general election takes place on November 3rd, 2026.
###

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1219?t=1001&akid=3067%2E251025%2EbXCooy ]Abdul for US Senate [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1219?t=1002&akid=3067%2E251025%2EbXCooy ]Abdul for US Senate

Hey Peter,

If you haven’t already, you’ll likely start seeing MAGA Republicans use my
full name a lot more in the coming weeks: Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed.

Donald Trump has already started using it as if it’s a punchline. ̄\_(
ツ)_/ ̄

Peter, I’ve
spent the majority of my career being someone who’s relatively young,
relatively brown, and relatively Muslim. Something I’ve learned along the
way is that when someone reaches for your name instead of your record,
it's because your record is the thing they can't touch:

* I’ve helped make government agencies actually work for Michiganders —
first by rebuilding Detroit’s Health Department after bankruptcy, and
then restructuring Wayne County’s Department of Health, Human &
Veterans Services.
* As a public servant, I’ve removed lead from elementary schools, taken
on Michigan’s biggest polluters, and made life-saving Narcan
universally accessible.

There’s nothing for them to attack there — so that’s why they’re resorting
to a politics rooted in hatred instead.

Meanwhile, Mike Rogers has a record he'd rather Michiganders never look at
too closely:

* Mike Rogers voted to raise his own pay in Congress.
* He championed a bill that helped create the opioid crisis.
* Then, after spending 15 years in Washington, he left and got $14
million richer working for the corporations he used to regulate and
moved to Florida.

And that’s why Mike Rogers needs $51,000,000+ worth of help to have a
chance at beating us in November.

We’re never going to outraise $51 million, but we don’t have to. We just
need folks like you to pitch in $10 to help us respond to
their attacks and get our message in front of as many Michiganders as
possible. If we do that, we will win. [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260831-1-ak.j0f2Su&amount=10&refcode=em20260831-3067&t=1004&akid=3067%2E251025%2EbXCooy ]Can I count on your support,
Peter?

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260831-1-ak.j0f2Su&amount=10&refcode=em20260831-3067&t=1023&akid=3067%2E251025%2EbXCooy ]Donate $10 ››

In solidarity,

Abdul

Hi friend, There are only 9 days until the primary. That means 9 days to reach the thousands of voters who are still undecided. 9 more days to convince Rhode Islanders that the Lieutenant Governor's office really can be a place of action, if we elect a leader with strong progressive values, a proven track record of delivering results, and a clear plan for the work that needs to be done. **And 9 more days to show that I am the only candidate ready to fight for Rhode Islanders.** I've asked a lot of you all over the past few months, and cannot even begin to express my gratitude for all the ways you have chipped in. Thank you for believing in a better Rhode Island, and for putting your trust in me to get us there. I have been working as hard as I can to earn the trust of voters all around the state. But, with only 9 days left and thousands of more voters still to reach, I still need your help to get us over the finish line. My dear friend Aaron Regunberg joined me at an event recently, where he told the audience that change really is possible, but that it won't just happen accidentally. **We all need to do our part to make it happen**. I know you all lead busy lives, and I know that sometimes it doesn't feel like one person can make that big of a difference. But if you really do believe in the potential for what Rhode Island is capable of, **now** is the time to take an extra step to make that potential a reality. **There are 4 key goals we need to hit in the last 9 days:**

body:
#

❗ Friends — To everyone who cares about ending the gun violence in our country, please don’t click away. This is an important August update from GIFFORDS. 👋
In a huge win for the gun lobby, Donald Trump just promised national right-to-carry legislation. This is the most extreme legislation we’ve seen in years, and we need your help to fight back.

You deserve an explanation:
This proposal, a concealed carry mandate, would make all of us less safe.
Currently, all 50 states and D.C. have the power to decide and implement their own laws about who can carry loaded, concealed handguns in public. _This legislation would allow states with the weakest laws to set the standard for all states._

That means someone from a state with no rules about who can buy or carry weapons could come into your town or neighborhood with a gun — and there’s nothing you could do to stop them.
Police leaders across the country have warned that these laws make their jobs nearly impossible._But the gun industry doesn’t care...as long as they can sell more guns._
There are already reports saying that the gun lobby may have enough votes in Congress to make it law, but there’s still time to speak out.

With less than 75 days until the November election, GIFFORDS is working around-the-clock to stop dangerous legislation like this and defeat the gun lobby’s endorsed candidates. All of that takes resources, which is why we need your help.
**Please make a contribution to GIFFORDS PAC right now.** Your donations will be put to work defeating dangerous legislation like this and electing gun safety leaders up and down the ballot.

How socialism takes over

|

Friend,

Socialism doesn’t take over a country overnight – but it can spiral out of control if the signs aren’t seen.

**First, it starts with promises.**

Free programs. Economic equality. Government protection. Politicians claim that surrendering “just a little more freedom” will make life easier for everyone.

**Next, it starts to spiral.**

More government spending creates more debt.
More debt weakens the economy and drives prices higher.
More instability becomes an excuse for higher taxes, heavier regulations, and even more government control over what people earn, own, and build.

And when those policies inevitably fail, socialist politicians never admit they were wrong.

**Then, they demand more power.**

Every time socialism is tried, political elites gain more control while ordinary families become poorer, more dependent, and less free.

**_Now, the Radical Left wants to bring those same failed ideas to America._**

They want Washington to control more of our economy, redistribute what hardworking Americans earn, and decide how you are allowed to spend your own money.
