Fellow Conservative,

I never thought I'd write you a letter like this.

But the day has come.

[A new poll from _Fox News_ shows we're DOWN by **3 POINTS.**](https://elink20c.newsletter.joinjustthetruth.com/ss/c/u001._iltqNytX8R9_iqLaPZU6zvdjLjeZKIt1tT_uPEbTC3W-zS2lyATZJlSPh40TJMDyQya4nww7Tjj0Ee1s4_9HhkraD0Bqjy0a-RvX7hhS6bCpqi1IrbPB1PhXmjZkrJ-4o3PH0WhKSZUQ8CA44gjNvTqfAbt7WxAlZkn5lIZWtXxnnTPKPc7b2uop3VeN1c2J9TifNGRzLIroxoagix_UgVVpeY9btSsyexdDG_tTuK08TJPVqpNJ_SlZ52acVDkot0SiWN0cicixRNFN6PXjlIB7hjI4oscrtavT5Zh-ZpbPBQA_y2qpETG9w3UAW0PEI7hJgDZamp8c78UfDtKL6N6D130yuYKm0gzT28iRgcitYOFvwSacFq2ZqkTlnJrLdejZZXBwitrtqvUkOhvebnandtqPHg_Iept1fQtjUVeXT1n30qcig6Umkp_oZgg/4tn/33S9Q1caQtabb_rjT_loUw/h2/h001.jUuZOZmZdjI2vMFuMLoWXgDlJ9NAfbujHpzvrCGJbr4)

All last month, we were DEADLOCKED in a tie at 47% - 47%. We were holding on for dear life despite being outraised and outspent.

[**But at some point, the numbers win. Math doesn't lie.**](https://elink20c.newsletter.joinjustthetruth.com/ss/c/u001._iltqNytX8R9_iqLaPZU6zvdjLjeZKIt1tT_uPEbTC3W-zS2lyATZJlSPh40TJMDyQya4nww7Tjj0Ee1s4_9HhkraD0Bqjy0a-RvX7hhS6bCpqi1IrbPB1PhXmjZkrJ-4o3PH0WhKSZUQ8CA44gjNvTqfAbt7WxAlZkn5lIZWtXxnnTPKPc7b2uop3VeN1c2J9TifNGRzLIroxoagix_UgVVpeY9btSsyexdDG_tTuK08TJPVqpNJ_SlZ52acVDkot0SiWN0cicixRNFN6PXjlIB7hjI4oscrtavT5Zh-ZpbPBQA_y2qpETG9w3UAW0PEI7hJgDZamp8c78UfDtKL6N6D130yuYKm0gzT28iRgcitYOFvwSacFq2ZqkTlnJrDjlZTf_zlkhUnZZY_LDWj-LJwDHTJBAQ-Sv3tLpht64iuelxDEgUFf_UljysFn12/4tn/33S9Q1caQtabb_rjT_loUw/h3/h001.EMm4K5I-nZRIl3b-zQXGv0wZW382EZ_poIdarTQAtQI)

[**Talarico has $21.5 million in the bank. We've got $6.9 million.**](https://elink20c.newsletter.joinjustthetruth.com/ss/c/u001._iltqNytX8R9_iqLaPZU6zvdjLjeZKIt1tT_uPEbTC3W-zS2lyATZJlSPh40TJMDyQya4nww7Tjj0Ee1s4_9HhkraD0Bqjy0a-RvX7hhS6bCpqi1IrbPB1PhXmjZkrJ-4o3PH0WhKSZUQ8CA44gjNvTqfAbt7WxAlZkn5lIZWtXxnnTPKPc7b2uop3VeN1c2J9TifNGRzLIroxoagix_UgVVpeY9btSsyexdDG_tTuK08TJPVqpNJ_SlZ52acVDkot0SiWN0cicixRNFN6PXjlIB7hjI4oscrtavT5Zh-ZpbPBQA_y2qpETG9w3UAW0PEI7hJgDZamp8c78UfDtKL6N6D130yuYKm0gzT28iRgcitYOFvwSacFq2ZqkTlnJrFEaSSgvYdLvpLPFb_ChTxWVMeIbRqdcFOhq1gZX6j77EmIB-nuOOyLy-i7_2WTCS/4tn/33S9Q1caQtabb_rjT_loUw/h4/h001.ACpXnpNK9jcqGyetaKeiYeyYA_-GAYaQ08AMYnuaEyo)

Those are the cold, hard facts of our race.

body:

Peter,
Over the last several days, people from across Central New York have answered our call.
They’ve contributed what they could. They’ve shared our message. They’ve shown that they believe this district is worth fighting for.
Now, we’ve reached the final test...
**Our End-of-Month deadline is at midnight TONIGHT!**

_**Control of Congress could determine whether President Trump can finish the job—or whether Democrats spend the next two years blocking his agenda, launching investigations, and dragging our country backward.**_
**I’m running to give President Trump another reliable America First vote in the House.**
I’ll vote to secure the border, cut wasteful spending, lower energy costs, defend our constitutional rights, and put American families first.
And when AOC, the DSA, and the Democrat establishment come after Central New York’s values, I won’t back down. **I’ll fight back.**
_But none of that happens unless we build a campaign capable of winning._
Your contribution tonight will help us reach more voters, organize more volunteers, keep our messages on the air, and prepare for the tough battles ahead.

subject: Something I still believe.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY BELL FOR MISSOURI
body:
64 days out, Peter. Peter,

I've spent most of my life here in St. Louis.

I grew up in North County, the son of a police officer and a county civil servant. I worked multiple jobs to put myself through college, went to law school, and came home to become a public defender.

Years later, when protests erupted just blocks from my home in Ferguson, I showed up. I stood with my neighbors, and in the years that followed, I worked to reform systems that had lost the trust of too many people in our community. None of that was part of some grand plan to end up in Congress.

_**I did it because this is my home, these are my neighbors, and this is the place I love.**_

But I've always believed that when you have the opportunity to make things better, you have a responsibility to try. That belief has taken me from the courtroom, to the Ferguson City Council, to the St. Louis County Prosecutor's Office, and _now to Congress._

It's been the honor of a lifetime getting to represent St. Louis in the House. Now, just **64 days out from Election Day,** and at midnight tonight, we close the books on a critical end-of-month fundraising deadline for August, and right now, we're still short of our goal.

Chip in before midnight to help us close the gap and make sure we have what it takes to keep fighting for this community >> **[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/bell-q3-2026?refcode2=dpwillis67@gmail.com](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138229462/643526296/114933226?refcode=em26_260831_EOM3_fnd_gq_act___WB_ettx&utm_campaign=em26_260831_EOM3_fnd_gq_act___WB_ettx&utm_medium=email&refcode2=aef1960d-47a5-f111-9b33-0022482a9a8d&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDYzODkiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYWVmMTk2MGQtNDdhNS1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5YThkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=A8nB6xTx_LqkY7hSiSUEIQLRK20TXmbMXFvghFkDo4A=)**

—Wesley

name: Roy Cooper
subject: I cannot possibly overstate this
body:
If there were a way to win a U.S. Senate seat without ever asking for donations, I’d do it in a heartbeat.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1118&source=&t=1&akid=3074%2E124072%2EVH4s45) | | | |
---
I don’t normally speak in superlatives, Peter, but there are two things that are impossible for me to overstate:
1) How desperate right-wing billionaires and corporate megadonors are to defeat us.
2) How much I dislike asking folks for their hard-earned money.
If there were a way to win a U.S. Senate seat without ever asking for donations, I’d do it in a heartbeat. But the fact that the GOP megadonor class can spend unlimited money – _and already is_ – to try to buy North Carolina for Trump’s hand-picked candidate makes it unrealistic.
[**_So if you get the problem and are willing to help us tackle it head-on, I hope you’ll consider chipping in today. We have until midnight to reach our most ambitious end-of-month goal yet of the entire campaign, and we still have a ways to go._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1118&amount=5&t=8&akid=3074%2E124072%2EVH4s45)
The thing is, Big Money is why so much in Washington DC is broken nowadays. Too often, politicians opt to take the easy route: fall in line, accept massive checks – with strings attached – to win elections, and then do as they’re told to keep the cash flowing. _All the while, the voices of the working people who voted them in continue to go unheard._
**North Carolinians don’t have to settle for that.**
Those at the top are terrified of what can happen when people understand their collective power to fundamentally change the system. What can happen when elections are no longer for sale.
Our people-powered campaign can overcome nearly $100 million so far in dark money and flip this seat blue for the first time since 2008. And it will be nothing short of a political earthquake.
So while I truly loathe asking you for money, I am going to because I know that transforming our politics by taking back North Carolina – and with it, the Senate majority – is worth it:
[**_Please Peter, will you contribute $5 or any amount you can spare to help us get the rest of the way to our $2 million goal? If we plan on winning this seat and fixing what’s broken in Washington DC, then we can’t afford to fall short tonight._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1118&amount=5&t=9&akid=3074%2E124072%2EVH4s45)
_If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_ | | | [DONATE $5](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14275?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1118&amount=5&t=10&akid=3074%2E124072%2EVH4s45)

| [OTHER AMOUNT](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1118&t=13&akid=3074%2E124072%2EVH4s45)
---
Thanks so much, Peter.
Roy Cooper
| |
* * *
[](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1118&t=2&akid=3074%2E124072%2EVH4s45)
Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

[**_Donate today to help win this seat and flip the Senate blue._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1118&source=&t=3&akid=3074%2E124072%2EVH4s45)

name: Kamala Harris
subject: This race will decide the Senate
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Pappas for Senate
body:
Chris Pappas knows how to win tough fights.
[](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260831_1.GhZRO6&refcode=em20260831-1&t=1&akid=8634%2E582294%2EoeAM7C)
Hi, it’s Kamala Harris.
The United States Senate is our most critical line of defense to put a real check on Donald Trump’s power, protect our democracy, and build an economy where every person has a fair shot. And we can’t flip the Senate without winning in New Hampshire. **That is why I am so proud to endorse Chris Pappas in his race for the U.S. Senate in New Hampshire.**
Chris Pappas is the fighter New Hampshire families need to take on rising costs, rampant corruption in Washington, and Donald Trump’s reckless administration. Chris knows how to get things done, and he’ll work with anyone to make life better for his fellow Granite Staters.
The outcome of this race could determine our ability to protect our progress and deliver for working families.
**The stakes could not be higher:[Will you make a $5 contribution to Chris’s campaign today, before his upcoming monthly fundraising deadline?](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260831_1.GhZRO6&refcode=em20260831-1&t=2&akid=8634%2E582294%2EoeAM7C)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260831_1.GhZRO6&amount=5&refcode=em20260831-1&t=21&akid=8634%2E582294%2EoeAM7C)**
Let me explain why your support in Chris’s race is so important right now:
New Hampshire remains one of the tightest battlegrounds in the country. In 2016, Maggie Hassan won by just 1,017 votes — making this open Senate seat a top target for national Republicans and MAGA special interests.
They are already throwing millions of dollars into New Hampshire to flip this seat red and send another rubber stamp for Trump to Washington. But Chris knows how to win tough fights. Time and again he has delivered for Granite State families by taking on corruption, focusing on lower costs, and protecting fundamental freedoms.
**[So if you’re ready to pitch in and help Chris Pappas win in November, will you contribute $5 or whatever you can to his campaign today?](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260831_1.GhZRO6&refcode=em20260831-1&t=22&akid=8634%2E582294%2EoeAM7C)**

We know that the real power is with the people, and we are most effective when we stand together.
Thank you for stepping up for Chris today to rebuild a government that truly serves its people.
Kamala

body:
[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/14176?t=1001&akid=1830%2E181023%2ESfNohu ]Jocelyn Benson sitting at a table, smiling while looking off screen.

I’ll be
direct: this is a fundraising email, and at the end of this message, I’m
going to ask you to chip in before our August end-of-month deadline at
midnight tonight.

But first, I want to explain to you how the
generosity of
supporters
like you made an impact this August. [ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/14176?t=1002&akid=1830%2E181023%2ESfNohu ]And when I’m done,
I hope you’ll consider making your first donation today.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/14176?t=1003&akid=1830%2E181023%2ESfNohu ]Donate →

FIRST: We won our primary election, receiving the most votes of any
candidate in Michigan statewide primary history.

Our victory earlier this month sends a strong message to John James,
Donald Trump, and anyone who’s looking to take our movement down this
November: we aren’t going anywhere.

And, the
only way we were able to build a movement as strong, as powerful, and as
resilient as this one is because
supporters
like you chipped in what they could, when they could, to get ads on the
air, volunteers knocking on doors, and supporters registered to vote.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/14176?t=1004&akid=1830%2E181023%2ESfNohu ]Your donation today helps us keep up our momentum as Election Day gets
closer →

THEN: We launched our first television ads of the general election,
reaching undecided voters all across Michigan.

This was a huge step for our campaign. For many Michiganders,
this ad is an introduction to our campaign, the future we’re fighting for,
and what’s at stake this November.

But Michigan’s media market is only getting more expensive — and with
far-right megadonors lining my opponent’s pockets, we need to make sure we
have the funds to keep our ads on the air and respond to any attacks.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/14176?t=1005&akid=1830%2E181023%2ESfNohu ]Your donation today helps us keep our ads on the air and reaching
undecided voters all across the state →

NOW: With our ticket finally set, we’re entering the final sprint towards
Election Day.

I have been so thrilled to have my friend and Senate Majority Leader
Winnie Brinks join me on the campaign trail as Michigan’s next Lieutenant
Governor. She’s the right partner to help lead Michigan forward — and
together, we’ve been hearing from voters all over the state about the need
for good governance, lower costs, and higher wages.

But after this deadline, Winnie and I will have just about two months to
spread our message all across Michigan, defend our campaign from
inevitable far-right attacks, rally our supporters, and make sure Michigan

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. name: Christina (personal)
subject: I almost lost my voice
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY CHRISTINA BOHANNAN FOR CONGRESS
body:
| Peter, there are a lot of different challenges that come with the first day of school.

I've heard from preschool teachers who spend the first week consoling children who are away from their parents for the very first time. Middle school teachers who have to figure out a way to make pre-teens care about grammar and punctuation. And as a law school professor, I spend those first days establishing a sense of professionalism and preparing my students for what will probably be the heaviest workload of their lives.

But there are two things that unite educators at almost every level. One is a deep love and concern for our students. The other is that we often have to talk A LOT.

By the end of the first week of teaching, I often feel that my vocal cords are on fire, my voice disappears, and I learn that whispering actually *makes it worse.*

**_For me, the last few months have been a little different._ Instead of preparing to teach, I’ve been knocking doors and talking to Iowans on the campaign trail. That's a lot of talking, and it finally caught up to me a few weeks ago. I nearly lost my voice again, but I didn't let a little hoarseness stop me.**

On the campaign trail, I drank my body weight in water, ate a ton of questionably-flavored cough drops, and got right back to work. Some things are worth losing your voice over. For me, this campaign is one of them.

I'm running because I want to be a voice for the people of IA-01. Representing this district isn't just about standing at a podium and talking. It's about making sure Iowans actually feel heard. That's why I've spent so much time listening to people in their communities and talking with them about what they want from the person who represents them in Congress.

| | | **What counts as a _suspended voter_?** In Texas, it means that the voter’s county doesn’t know their address or thinks they’ve moved. It doesn’t necessarily stop people from voting in November’s midterm elections, but it does make the process of voting much more difficult. If a voter shows up on Election Day and their registration is suspended, they have to fill out a “ _statement of residence_ ” form, and if they’ve moved to a new county, they’ll either be required to vote in their old one or **be given a provisional ballot** , according to _The Dallas Morning News_. Just to be clear: **The rates of rejection on provisional ballots are substantially higher than mail-in ballots**. They are easier to question, easier to challenge and get thrown out, which is why we're trying to reach every eligible voter we can to have their registration verified to be valid for the upcoming election. There should be no doubt about how scared opponents of voting rights are if they're suddenly willing to go to these new extremes to pick and choose whose vote gets to count in the midterms. And elections are routinely decided by less than six percentage points.This is especially critical when Texas's upcoming Senate race is one of the most-watched and forecast as one of the tightest elections this November. # **Karoline Leavitt says she 's advising Trump on her press secretary successor**
In her final interview as White House press secretary, Karoline Leavitt **[revealed she's been privately advising Trump](https://substack.com/redirect/e3bb60b2-320b-4c75-ac08-e4f53cec2309?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** on candidates to replace her, noting there's "no shortage" of interest in the role but declining to name potential picks.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e3bb60b2-320b-4c75-ac08-e4f53cec2309?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Leavitt said the most essential quality for the next press secretary is Trump 's full trust,** given the close working relationship the role requires, and said she hopes to remain involved in the decision if Trump wants her input.
* **Leavitt called her departure "bittersweet,"** praising her nearly 20 months serving Trump as the "adventure of a lifetime" as she steps back to spend more time with her two young children, describing Trump as both a supportive boss and friend throughout the process.

# **DSA 's agenda could cost more than $200 trillion, CATO report**
A new Cato Institute report estimates the Democratic Socialists of America's policy wishlist -- including universal health care, reparations, and a federal jobs guarantee -- could **[cost over $200 trillion over the next decade,](https://substack.com/redirect/64366205-1408-432f-bf83-d341e21a1f6e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** pushing government spending to as much as 57% to 92% of GDP, compared to roughly 34% in 2025.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/64366205-1408-432f-bf83-d341e21a1f6e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Report author Adam Michel argues DSA 's plan to fund these programs through wealth and corporate taxes falls far short:** seizing the top 400 Americans' entire net worth would cover only 3-9% of the estimated costs, while projected corporate profits would fund roughly half the low-end estimate.
* **DSA co-chair Megan Romer struggled to define the group 's "tax the rich" strategy** in a recent New Yorker Radio Hour interview, unable to offer specifics when pressed by host David Remnick.

# **9/11 cancer cases surge nearly 17-fold over past decade**
Cancer certifications among 9/11 survivors and responders jumped from 3,204 in 2015 to 57,044 this year, **[according to World Trade Center Health Program data,](https://substack.com/redirect/6a4cc890-c116-4785-9b2f-0a61717014df?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** with survivors' cases now outpacing those of emergency responders for the first time.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6a4cc890-c116-4785-9b2f-0a61717014df?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Rare cancers are increasingly common among the group,** including thymus, neuroendocrine, male breast, and brain cancers; 67% of the program's 145,275 members are certified for at least one of 69 linked cancers, far above the national average. Officials attribute part of the rise to the aging population of those exposed.
* **More than 9,425 people have now died from post-9/11 illnesses,** over triple the original attack's death toll. Attorney Michael Barasch, who represents thousands in the program, urged more civilians exposed to Ground Zero toxins to enroll, noting only about 15% currently have.

# **Google Maps now shows "Lake America" for US users**
Google Maps has begun **[displaying"Lake America"](https://substack.com/redirect/14e67c2b-4e25-4ddd-8959-c039caa05de2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** instead of Lake Ontario for U.S. users, following the U.S. Geographic Names Information System's formal update after Trump signed an executive order renaming the lake last Thursday, citing its economic importance to the country.
* **Google said the change reflects its policy of following official government naming sources,** meaning Canadian users will still see "Lake Ontario" while those outside both countries will see both names.
* **The renaming comes amid escalating U.S.-Canada trade tensions,** with 50% U.S. tariffs on roughly $20 billion in Canadian goods taking effect Aug. 22 after talks broke down, and Canada set to impose retaliatory tariffs on a similar amount of U.S. imports starting Sept. 8.

His episode of __[_I Serve_](https://us.list-manage.com/SJoaF_CBc0j?e=33f53a5b1a&c2id=cb2f151404272f38c482059c4a3ef720), a podcast co-produced by Foreign Policy and With Honor, takes listeners inside those defining moments, from armored combat in the Gulf War to his time in the West Wing.
Each episode follows one service member through a mission that tested their limits, and through the standards that they carried long after leaving the field.
It's one of ten episodes now available in season one, including With Honor's Co-Founder and CEO Rye Barcott ("The Founder"), plus fellow Advisory Board members General Nadja West ("The Surgeon General") and Elliot Ackerman ("The Special Operator").

### More Time, Less Pressure: The GRACE for Military Survivors Act
---
| | | | | | | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/rH_hiGajURL?e=33f53a5b1a&c2id=cb2f151404272f38c482059c4a3ef720)
| |
_Reps. Mike Thompson and Jack Bergman at the For Country Caucus Memorial Day Vietnam Memorial cleaning._
---
| |
For military families grieving the loss of a loved one, the last thing they need is a ticking clock on major financial decisions. The GRACE Act would make sure they don't have to choose between grieving and planning.
For Country Caucus members Reps. Mike Thompson and Jack Bergman, both Vietnam War veterans, introduced the Granting Rollover Access and Contribution Extensions (GRACE) for Military Survivors Act (H.R. 9489) earlier this summer, alongside Reps. Greg Steube and Juan Vargas.
The legislation would give surviving families three years, instead of just one, to decide whether to roll death gratuities and Service Members' Group Life Insurance payouts into Roth IRAs and Coverdell Education Savings Accounts without penalty, recognizing that sound financial planning takes time these families shouldn't be denied.

body:
An issue a day

| |
---
| | _With just eight days until the primary, I am using each day to discuss an issue I have highlighted on the campaign trail. For Day 8, I am highlighting the need to regulate AI before it’s too late._
* * *
Dear David, You can’t pay for parking, get into a movie, or do basic tasks without your phone. AI is accelerating this problem: it is being used to deny people healthcare, replace workers, surveil communities, and make military decisions that should require human judgment. Our lives have become beholden to the priorities and profits of technology corporations, and we never had a say in it. **[Whether we like it or not, AI is here to stay. But we can take several steps to regulate AI and hold powerful tech companies accountable _now_ , before they gain even more control over our lives. If you’re ready to support this work, please pitch in today:](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/3fJItPAaiUJaC8Qdy0WQfA~~/AAUS1hA~/vIzjlS3XNfELPtXTuPr5cvPn-Mo0wHiOkCIpir_I40jYKfCCo-JS6YNoTJt7FWEnsiZZFbJvOpzPvYsgGJ8LuU5xnY6g_pJlvA3Xui2UOV_QZ_sbmPQKUZQY5n5w5zfpyBdAqjNSyRZhMrBJP4DLVY3Hk_etKf_aCL5KbrZDOQdoJrSujsDo3gXsuwHFj4tDNruWiyNwtsxQ5Ojy2lJzMLvmj22LaazdjJoi3DZ7wc5AELIpW_03Snx3c2-zUsJBMI-EpzHRE0AUlK3CKy4RyQ~~)** | | [DONATE](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/3fJItPAaiUJaC8Qdy0WQfA~~/AAUS1hA~/vIzjlS3XNfELPtXTuPr5cvPn-Mo0wHiOkCIpir_I40jYKfCCo-JS6YNoTJt7FWEnsiZZFbJvOpzPvYsgGJ8LuU5xnY6g_pJlvA3Xui2UOV_QZ_sbmPQKUZQY5n5w5zfpyBdAqjNSyRZhMrBJP4DLVY3Hk_etKf_aCL5KbrZDOQdoJrSujsDo3gXsuwHFj4tDNruWiyNwtsxQ5Ojy2lJzMLvmj22LaazdjJoi3DZ7wc5AELIpW_03Snx3c2-zUsJBMI-EpzHRE0AUlK3CKy4RyQ~~)
---
AI is being used to deny people healthcare, replace workers, surveil communities, and make military decisions that should require human judgment. **And to make matters worse, the companies building these systems have amassed so much power that they can pay for whatever laws they want.**
We’ve seen this story before: Social media companies were allowed to grow for twenty years without any meaningful regulation, and we’re just now starting to see accountability for these companies _decades_ after they’ve been allowed to wreak havoc on our public health and democracy.
We know the dangers of AI, and we can take action now to prevent harms from occurring in the first place rather than waiting twenty years for class action lawsuits to deliver justice. But here’s the problem: Shady AI super PACs are pouring millions of dollars into races across the country to elect politicians who will serve their interests, not those of the American people.
**That’s why we need lawmakers in Congress who will reject corporate PAC money and fight for comprehensive AI regulation that protects workers, patients, and consumers.**
That means prohibiting AI in the nuclear weapons program, requiring transparency when AI is used to make decisions about people’s healthcare or employment, enacting real data privacy protections, and ensuring that Congress has meaningful oversight before these technologies are deployed in ways that affect people’s lives.
It means putting a moratorium on data center construction until we have legislation that requires these companies to address and offset the impact of new data centers on public health, the environment, and energy prices.
And it means breaking up these monopolies so that a few giant tech companies that are too big to fail don’t have complete control over every aspect of our lives.
**[I refuse to surrender to Big Tech billionaires like Elon Musk and Mark Zuckerberg. That’s why I don’t pay to advertise on their platforms or spend my time chasing likes and clicks on their platforms. And it’s why I’m putting regulating the tech industry at the top of my agenda in Congress. Can you help me take this fight to Washington by pitching in today?](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/3fJItPAaiUJaC8Qdy0WQfA~~/AAUS1hA~/vIzjlS3XNfELPtXTuPr5cvPn-Mo0wHiOkCIpir_I40jYKfCCo-JS6YNoTJt7FWEnsiZZFbJvOpzPvYsgGJ8LuU5xnY6g_pJlvA3Xui2UOV_QZ_sbmPQKUZQY5n5w5zfpyBdAqjNSyRZhMrBJP4DLVY3Hk_etKf_aCL5KbrZDOQdoJrSujsDo3gXsuwHFj4tDNruWiyNwtsxQ5Ojy2lJzMLvmj22LaazdjJoi3DZ7wc5AELIpW_03Snx3c2-zUsJBMI-EpzHRE0AUlK3CKy4RyQ~~)**

clean_body: An issue a day | | | | With just eight days until the primary, I am using each day to discuss an issue I have highlighted on the campaign trail. For Day 8, I am highlighting the need to regulate AI before it’s too late. Dear David, You can’t pay for parking, get into a movie, or do basic tasks without your phone. AI is accelerating this problem: it is being used to deny people healthcare, replace workers, surveil communities, and make military decisions that should require human judgment. Our lives have become beholden to the priorities and profits of technology corporations, and we never had a say in it. ~~ | | ~~ AI is being used to deny people healthcare, replace workers, surveil communities, and make military decisions that should require human judgment. And to make matters worse, the companies building these systems have amassed so much power that they can pay for whatever laws they want. We’ve seen this story before: Social media companies were allowed to grow for twenty years without any meaningful regulation, and we’re just now starting to see accountability for these companies decades after they’ve been allowed to wreak havoc on our public health and democracy. We know the dangers of AI, and we can take action now to prevent harms from occurring in the first place rather than waiting twenty years for class action lawsuits to deliver justice. But here’s the problem: Shady AI super PACs are pouring millions of dollars into races across the country to elect politicians who will serve their interests, not those of the American people. That’s why we need lawmakers in Congress who will reject corporate PAC money and fight for comprehensive AI regulation that protects workers, patients, and consumers. That means prohibiting AI in the nuclear weapons program, requiring transparency when AI is used to make decisions about people’s healthcare or employment, enacting real data privacy protections, and ensuring that Congress has meaningful oversight before these technologies are deployed in ways that affect people’s lives. It means putting a moratorium on data center construction until we have legislation that requires these companies to address and offset the impact of new data centers on public health, the environment, and energy prices. And it means breaking up these monopolies so that a few giant tech companies that are too big to fail don’t have complete control over every aspect of our lives. ~~ If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | ~ ~ | ~ | ~~ We’re in a race for our future. | | **_Meet Russell:_** Born and raised in Surfside Beach, SC, Congressman Russell Fry is the proud and homegrown Representative for South Carolina’s 7th Congressional District. Growing up in a cinder block home with no heating or air conditioning, Russell learned at an early age that hard work and perseverance pave the only true path to the American Dream. He watched his parents work day in and day out to make ends meet. And the values they instilled in him during his upbringing led Russell to self-fund both his undergraduate education at the University of South Carolina, and later his law studies at the Charleston School of Law. At Charleston, Russell served as the President of the Student Bar Association and even helped the school achieve its American Bar Association accreditation. He went on to practice law in the Grand Strand area for over a decade before entering the political arena to serve in the South Carolina House of Representatives for State House District 106 (Horry County). During his seven-year tenure in the SC House, Russell fought to safeguard Constitutional liberties, lower taxes, and put the best interests of South Carolina families above all else. He climbed the ranks to become Chief Majority Whip, and also chaired the House Opioid Prevention Study Committee. Under Russell’s leadership, 18 policy initiatives to combat the opioid crisis were signed into law. Since the first day he stepped foot in Washington, Russell has strived to shake up the corrupt status quo and deliver real change for the American people. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation. Russell is a dedicated husband to his wife, Bronwen, and a loving father to his son, James. The family lives in Murrells Inlet with their chocolate lab, Jasper.

If this is the company Chris Pappas wants to keep, Granite Staters should be concerned.Harris was tasked by the Biden administration with addressing the root causes of migration from Central America. Sorry if that was an ominous subject line, Peter. But as of today, we’re really getting there. Our campaign and Mike Lawler are both trading TV ads, and tomorrow we kick off our final quarterly FEC deadline month. The end is, truthfully, nigh. But we won’t lie to you, we’ve got a lot of work to do between now and November, if we want to beat Mike Lawler and take back the House. New York is the single most expensive place in the country to run a political campaign – add in that this is going to be the most competitive House race in the country, and we have some seriously ambitious fundraising goals. Now, if everyone reading this email chipped in just $17, we’d CRUSH those goals. We would be on track to put out a historic FEC report, and would be well on our way toward funding a winning operation. But most folks won’t chip in. We’re hoping you’re different. Because if we’re going to win this crucial battleground race, we’re going to need the biggest team possible. Please. [Can you chip in $17, or any amount, right now? # Iran
* **U.S. resumes strikes on Iran, hitting Larak Island:** U.S. forces [struck](https://substack.com/redirect/a99dfc51-88ec-463c-a6df-db83ed910f86?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Iran's Larak Island on Sunday, killing two Iranians and wounding two others. U.S. President Donald Trump paused military action in late July, claiming he had shelved plans for the "biggest attack since World War II" following appeals from Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the UAE, and saying talks with Iran were ongoing, amid reports at the time that U.S. Patriot interceptor stocks were depleted.
* U.S. forces claimed Iranian Revolutionary Guard (IRGC) troops were preparing to fire rockets carrying sea mines into the Strait of Hormuz from the island.
* A U.S. drone carried out the strike, according to Tasnim, an outlet affiliated with Iran's IRGC.
* The strike was the first known U.S. attack on Iran since late July.
* **Iran retaliates, striking U.S. base in Jordan:** Iran said it [fired](https://substack.com/redirect/b4475a34-6bec-42dd-8728-2bb540c21858?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ballistic missiles at two U.S. air bases in Jordan--the King Hussein (Mafraq) and Al-Azraq (Muwaffaq Salti) bases--with the IRGC claiming the strikes destroyed maintenance infrastructure and fighter jet deployment sites.
* Jordan said it intercepted eight missiles that entered its airspace, according to Al-Mamlaka TV.
* Trump [told](https://substack.com/redirect/7b491106-7631-44f5-be1f-b24f476e054f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Fox News on Monday morning that the U.S. would respond to the Jordan attack, in which he claimed all but one of the missiles were intercepted. "We're going to hit them hard," he said.
* **Iranian president says U.S. is not "keeping commitments": **Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said in response to the resumption of attacks that Iran "never welcomes war," but that his U.S counterparts had not "fulfilled their commitments."
* Pezeshkian made the remarks at a meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday. The two reportedly discussed maritime arrangements through the Strait of Hormuz, as well as cooperation at Iran's Chabahar port, where India has invested more than $120 million. A waiver on U.S. sanctions at the port expired on Sunday.
* **UAE says it intercepted an Iranian drone on Monday:** The United Arab Emirates [said](https://substack.com/redirect/794f5b59-85a5-4d9a-9424-e14f14226004?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Monday that it had "dealt with" an Iranian drone that had been detected over its waters in a statement from its Defense Ministry.
* The Iranian army claimed it had targeted the Al Minhad air base in Dubai. The UAE then issued a second statement denying that the base had been hit, calling such allegations "false."
* **Trump posts AI-generated video claiming Kharg Island attack; U.S. and Iran say no strike occurred:** A U.S. official denied Monday that forces had struck Iran's main oil export hub on Kharg Island, Reuters reported, after Trump [posted](https://substack.com/redirect/d5685ce8-6f8c-45b1-b681-06b85b07a6da?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an AI-generated video purporting to show the island being attacked. "Kharg Island being blown to smithereens," Trump wrote alongside the video on Truth Social.
* National Iranian Oil Company chief Hamid Bovard called Trump's post "laughable," and said conditions on the island were "calm and appropriate."
* Trump later declared that Iran was "officially a Failed Nation" and "DEAD" in another Truth Social [post](https://substack.com/redirect/f2c6ee42-5f7b-4bdf-a5fd-b97f6249703e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

Photo by Atta Kenare / AFP via Getty Images. Monday, August 31, 2026 - U.S. resumes strikes on Iran, hitting Larak Island. Iran retaliates, striking U.S. base in Jordan. Iranian president says U.S. is not "keeping commitments." UAE says it intercepted an Iranian drone on Monday. U.S. President Donald Trump posts AI-generated video claiming Kharg Island attack; U.S. and Iran say no strike occurred. Tanker hits mines in Strait of Hormuz, now ablaze. U.S. distillate fuel stocks at record seasonal low. Israeli strikes on Gaza kill five on Monday, wound fishermen. Israel continues attacks on Gaza over the weekend. Israeli settlers attack NBC crew, Palestinian woman. Israeli attacks hit three southern Lebanon districts despite "ceasefire." Federal judge rules Trump administration unconstitutionally targets critics of Israel for deportation. Israel evacuates Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's son from U.S. over "significant threat." Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed apologizes for comments about attack on synagogue. Trump administration proposes Yosemite land swap on behalf of developer. Pentagon secretly employs conservative influencers to promote War Secretary Pete Hegseth, attack critics. Ex-Ecuador president Lenin Moreno sentenced to 5 years for bribe scheme. Israel signs $3.5 billion air defense deal with Greece. South Africa submits dossier to ICJ on Israeli non-compliance in genocide case. Venezuela's acting president Delcy Rodriguez reveals details of U.S. oil deal. WSJ: Pentagon to take stake in Venezuelan oil venture. Russian strike hits transportation infrastructure in Danube grain hub. Ukraine's former defense minister seeks U.S. money for new weapons fund. UN Security Council convenes emergency meeting on Haiti. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran U.S. resumes strikes on Iran, hitting Larak Island: U.S. forces Iran's Larak Island on Sunday, killing two Iranians and wounding two others. U.S. President Donald Trump paused military action in late July, claiming he had shelved plans for the "biggest attack since World War II" following appeals from Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the UAE, and saying talks with Iran were ongoing, amid reports at the time that U.S. Patriot interceptor stocks were depleted. U.S. forces claimed Iranian Revolutionary Guard (IRGC) troops were preparing to fire rockets carrying sea mines into the Strait of Hormuz from the island. A U.S. drone carried out the strike, according to Tasnim, an outlet affiliated with Iran's IRGC. The strike was the first known U.S. attack on Iran since late July. Iran retaliates, striking U.S. base in Jordan: Iran said it ballistic missiles at two U.S. air bases in Jordan--the King Hussein (Mafraq) and Al-Azraq (Muwaffaq Salti) bases--with the IRGC claiming the strikes destroyed maintenance infrastructure and fighter jet deployment sites. Jordan said it intercepted eight missiles that entered its airspace, according to Al-Mamlaka TV. Trump Fox News on Monday morning that the U.S. would respond to the Jordan attack, in which he claimed all but one of the missiles were intercepted. "We're going to hit them hard," he said. Iranian president says U.S. is not "keeping commitments": Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said in response to the resumption of attacks that Iran "never welcomes war," but that his U.S counterparts had not "fulfilled their commitments." Pezeshkian made the remarks at a meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday. The two reportedly discussed maritime arrangements through the Strait of Hormuz, as well as cooperation at Iran's Chabahar port, where India has invested more than $120 million. A waiver on U.S. sanctions at the port expired on Sunday. UAE says it intercepted an Iranian drone on Monday: The United Arab Emirates on Monday that it had "dealt with" an Iranian drone that had been detected over its waters in a statement from its Defense Ministry. The Iranian army claimed it had targeted the Al Minhad air base in Dubai. The UAE then issued a second statement denying that the base had been hit, calling such allegations "false." Trump posts AI-generated video claiming Kharg Island attack; U.S. and Iran say no strike occurred: A U.S. official denied Monday that forces had struck Iran's main oil export hub on Kharg Island, Reuters reported, after Trump an AI-generated video purporting to show the island being attacked. "Kharg Island being blown to smithereens," Trump wrote alongside the video on Truth Social. National Iranian Oil Company chief Hamid Bovard called Trump's post "laughable," and said conditions on the island were "calm and appropriate." Trump later declared that Iran was "officially a Failed Nation" and "DEAD" in another Truth Social . Tanker hits mines in Hormuz, now ablaze: An oil tanker caught fire after hitting two sea mines while attempting to take an "illegal" route through the Strait of Hormuz, the IRGC reported on Monday. The statement did not provide details on casualties or the extent of the damage. The U.S.-led Joint Maritime Information Center Sunday there remains a "continued risk of drifting or uncharted mines" in and near the Strait of Hormuz's main traffic lanes, with mine danger areas still active. The Joint Maritime Information Center recorded 65 U.S.-facilitated Hormuz transits from August 27-29, compared with a historical baseline of roughly 138 vessels per day. Tanker struck by unknown projectile in Strait of Hormuz: A tanker was on Saturday by an unknown projectile while transiting inbound through the Strait of Hormuz, about 12 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman. No casualties or environmental impact were reported. The source of the projectile remains unknown. Iran has struck multiple vessels in the past month as the U.S. military seeks to continue the shuttle trade with dark transits going through the southern Omani route. Khamenei calls to phase out the U.S. dollar from Iran 's economy: Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei for gradually phasing the U.S. dollar out of Iran's economy and building a self-reliant "resistance economy" centered on domestic production, in a written message issued Saturday. He urged the government to tackle inflation, unemployment, and price controls, and to direct investment toward essential sectors. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent this past week issued additional sanctions against 60 new Iranian entities, aimed at completely severing Iran's economic ties worldwide. Oil prices spike after U.S. resumes strikes: Oil prices rose more than $1 a barrel Monday, pushing the war past its sixth month, Reuters . Brent surged past the $90 threshold to an intraday high of $91.52 a barrel, with US WTI crude climbing to $86.79. Palestine Killed and wounded in Gaza: Over the past 24 hours, two Palestinians were killed and 10 were injured in attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,456 killed, with 174,496 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,320 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 4,385, while 815 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble. Israeli strikes on Gaza kill five on Monday, wound fishermen: An Israeli strike on Gaza City on Monday three Palestinians in the Tel al-Hawa neighborhood of Gaza City, WAFA reported. A separate attack earlier on Monday killed two Palestinians west of Gaza City. Israeli warships on fishermen working off the coast of Gaza, injuring five. Israel continues attacks on Gaza over the weekend: Israeli forces nine Palestinians and wounded at least 18 across Gaza on Saturday. An Israeli drone struck a Palestinian delivery rider and his electric bicycle in southwestern Gaza City, killing the driver and wounding three others. Separately on Saturday, Israeli forces fired on Al-Masdar village, killing a Palestinian man, and Israeli tank and artillery fire hit eastern areas of Khan Younis, wounding two in Al-Mawasi. An Israeli quadcopter also dropped bombs near Kamal Adwan Hospital in Beit Lahia. On Sunday, an Israeli strike near a bakery in western Deir al-Balah killed a three-year-old Palestinian boy. Drop Site contributor Mohamed Ahmed reported from the site of the strike, speaking to the boy's relatives. His voice breaking, one relative said the boy was born after seven years of waiting. "Oh, Taim. You wanted Pringles. Taim, I promised you I'd bring you Pringles." Watch his dispatch. Israeli attacks on the occupied West Bank continue: Ramallah: Israeli soldiers shot and injured four Palestinians in the village of Al-Mughayyir on Sunday, after a heavy raid on the city, during which Israeli soldiers deployed tear gas against the residents of the area. Separately, Israeli** settlers a Palestinian family out of their home in the majority-Christian village of al-Taybeh on Monday, following a week of threats and attacks, WAFA reported. The settlers began circling the house in quad bikes last week, according to the owners, before attacking the house's entrance, attempting to steal their belongings and cutting their internet cables and fences. Nablus: Israeli settlers a Palestinian home in Qusra, south of Nablus on Saturday, hurling stones and entering through a window as Israeli soldiers stood nearby without intervening, Haaretz reported. Israeli soldiers later arrested the Palestinian residents of the home. On Monday, Israeli settlers a two-story Palestinian home in Nablus city, and Israeli forces a Palestinian man from the Balata refugee camp after a raid on a cafe in the area. East Jerusalem: Israeli forces the UNRWA Qalandiya Institute for Vocational Education for Refugees in Qalandiya once again Monday, after a raid on the facility last Tuesday provoked international condemnation. Jericho: Israeli forces the Aqaba Jabr refugee camp on Monday, prompting "clashes," according to WAFA. The soldiers reportedly fired stun grenades into the camp and pursued several Palestinian young men within. Jenin : Israeli settlers a new settlement, "Noa," on Palestinian land in the Jenin governorate, with Israeli ministers and Knesset members holding a ceremony at the site on Monday. Separately, in the town of Qabatiya, Israeli forces a Palestinian young man while he passed through a checkpoint, closing entrances into the village after doing so. Israel advances settlement expansion east of Jerusalem as Ben-Gvir leads settler incursion into Al-Aqsa: Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound on Monday under Israeli police protection, leading groups of settlers into the site, according to the Jerusalem Governorate. The Governorate condemned the incursion as a "dangerous escalation" and a violation of the historic and legal status quo at Al-Aqsa, warning of efforts to impose greater Israeli control over the mosque. Separately, Israeli authorities 370.28 dunams (91.5 acres) of land in Abu Dis and Arab al-Sawahra as "state property," according to the Wall and Settlement Resistance Commission. The move advances plans for the Mishmar Yehuda settlement in occupied East Jerusalem; the total land claimed by Israelis for the project is now about 3,750 dunams (927 acres). Israeli settlers attack NBC crew, Palestinian woman: On Saturday, a group of masked settlers armed with clubs a team of NBC correspondents and Aida Ahmed Abdullah, a 51-year-old Palestinian woman they were interviewing, in the occupied West Bank village of Jaldu, near Nablus. The attack left the woman unconscious, NBC correspondent Matt Bradley reported. Abdullah was describing to the network how settlers had recently forced her family out of their home. Bradley was struck twice in the arm, and the team's producer, cameraman, and driver all sustained injuries. The attack also heavily damaged the team's broadcast equipment. Lebanon Israeli attacks hit three southern Lebanon districts despite "ceasefire": Israeli forces carried out attacks across three districts of southern Lebanon overnight and on Monday despite the ceasefire. In Marjayoun, a series of powerful, successive Israeli explosions part of a mountain in Qantara to collapse, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. shows extensive damage to the side of the mountain. In Nabatieh, the Israeli military carried out a large explosion in the town of Arnoun, near the northern edge of Beaufort Castle. In Tyre (Sour), Israeli forces Mansouri and Buyout Al-Sayyad overnight and into the early morning hours. On Sunday, Israeli forces strikes on Douha Kfar Rumman, near Nabatieh, and al-Qantara in the Marjayoun district, Lebanese media reported. Israeli forces also fired phosphorus munitions around Kfar Tibnit and Nabatieh al-Fawqa. Airstrikes in at least five locations, artillery shelling across 10, and a drone strike near Nabatieh al-Fawqa were reported on Saturday by journalist Courtney Bonneau. U.S. News Federal judge rules Trump administration unconstitutionally targets critics of Israel for deportation : Judge No el Wise in San Jose that the Trump administration is unconstitutionally silencing noncitizen critics of Israel's Gaza war and others through its threats of deportation. Wise's Friday ruling follows a suit brought by The Stanford Daily, which had argued the policy chilled international students from speaking out against the genocide. Noncitizens at the paper had quit, withheld articles, refused assignments, requested articles be taken down, and asked for anonymity out of fear of deportation. Wise wrote that "the government has offered a chilling message regarding protected speech--speak out against Israel or in support of Palestinians and we will revoke your visa and deport you. U.S. deports dozens to Central African Republic, including Afghan protected from Taliban threats: The United States dozens of people to the Central African Republic on Saturday, including a group of 12 Afghans, eight Iranians, and several from Nepal and Nicaragua, according to the immigrants' rights group Human Rights First. The flight marks the second such deportation to the country since June. Among those deported was an Afghan man in his early twenties who had been granted protection against deportation to Afghanistan by a U.S. judge over fears of Taliban persecution, according to his lawyer. The man's family faced Taliban threats due to his brothers' collaboration with the U.S. military. ICE plans to purchase $2 million worth of "robot dogs": U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) is planning to spend up to $2 million on "robot dogs," according to a federal procurement notice by ABC News. Manufactured by Boston Dynamics, the robots will support "law enforcement operations," according to the notice. The news comes after ICE's decision earlier this month to purchase gloves that can deliver painful electric shocks. Israel evacuates Netanyahu 's son from U.S. over "significant threat": Israel's Shin Bet security agency it evacuated Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's oldest son, Yair Netanyahu , from the United States due to a "significant threat" against him. The agency did not elaborate on the nature or source of the threat. Yair, who moved to Miami in 2023 and remained abroad for much of Israel's wars in Gaza, Lebanon, and Iran, has often served as an unofficial adviser to his father. El-Sayed apologizes for comments about attack on synagogue: Abdul El-Sayed , the Democratic Senate nominee in Michigan, Saturday to the state's Jewish Democratic Caucus for a March statement about an attack on Temple Israel synagogue in West Bloomfield Township that included the phrase "hurt people hurt people," saying "if my statement caused pain, I'm sorry." Despite mounting pressure from pro-Israel groups and Democratic officials, El-Sayed declined to disavow streamer Hasan Piker , who campaigned with him during the primary: "I am not interested in a conversation about a social-media person in California." Trump administration proposes Yosemite land swap on behalf of developer: The Trump administration transferring a small parcel of land inside Yosemite National Park's western boundary to a company controlled by real estate firm Kingsbarn Realty Capital, whose CEO Jeff Pori donated more than $4,000 to Trump's 2024 campaign, in exchange for the firm purchasing equivalent-value land elsewhere in California for the Park Service, according to The New York Times. Kingsbarn wants the swap to build a road enabling access to two 40-acre parcels it bought near the park in 2024 for an "upscale" development of cabins and commercial buildings, a representative of the company told the Times. Pentagon secretly employs conservative influencers to promote Hegseth, attack critics: The Pentagon has quietly several conservative military veterans with large online followings into government roles, including retired colonels Rob Maness ,Kurt Schlichter , and Thomas Anderson , without disclosing their assignments, according to The Washington Post. Maness, Schlichter, and Anderson have published columns and social media posts defending Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and attacking military critics without disclosing their Pentagon ties. Maness and Schlichter, who have over 135,000 and nearly 620,000 X followers, respectively, hold active ".civ" government email addresses assigned to the office of Undersecretary of Defense Anthony Tata , though a Pentagon spokesman declined to say whether any are paid or detail their roles. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Ex-Ecuador president Len in Moreno sentenced to 5 years for bribe scheme: Former Ecuadorian President Lenin Moreno was in prison for his role in a $76 million bribery scheme involving Chinese state contractor Sinohydro and the construction of the massive Coca Codo Sinclair hydroelectric plant. The illicit kickbacks occurred while Moreno served as vice president (2007-2013) under socialist leader Rafael Correa. Though Moreno originally took office in 2017 with Correa's backing, he quickly broke with his predecessor's political legacy--making a sharp pivot to the right and aligning closely with Washington. Israel signs $3.5 billion air defense deal with Greece: Israel and Greece a $3.5 billion agreement under which Israel will build a multi-layered air defense system for Greece including its David's Sling system, one of the biggest export deals in Israel's history. Greece will become the second foreign customer for David's Sling after Finland. It will also receive a new command-and-control system developed by Rafael as part of a broader modernization effort to create an integrated air defense system. "This marks the first time the [Israeli Defense Ministry] will supply a complete defense array against a wide range of threats--from ballistic missiles and aerial threats to hostile unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs)," the Israeli Ministry of Defense said in a . South Africa submits dossier to ICJ on Israeli non-compliance in genocide case: South Africa a dossier of information to the International Court of Justice (ICJ) detailing Israel's continued non-compliance with legally binding provisional measures. The submission, officially handed over on August 25, serves to assist an ICJ committee of judges tasked with monitoring the implementation of the court's orders in Gaza to protect the rights of the Palestinian people under the Genocide Convention. Venezuela 's Rodriguez reveals details of U.S. oil deal: Venezuelan acting President Delcy Rodriguez publicly the 25-year energy agreement with the United States that opens the country's oil fields to US capital. The plan covers 17 strategic fields with 65 billion barrels of proven reserves, roughly a fifth of Venezuela's total, plus eight undeveloped "greenfield" blocks in the Orinoco Belt. Rodriguez framed the agreement as preserving "sovereignty," saying Venezuela retains ownership of its resources while inviting U.S. investment. She projected over $100 billion in investment and more than $209 billion in state tax revenue, with production targeted to exceed 1.5 million barrels per day. Chevron, which has operated in Venezuela for a century, is among the firms expected to finalize expanded stakes. Trump claimed on Sunday that Venezuelan oil would be used to replenish the U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve, which has been severely depleted due to the U.S. war with Iran. WSJ: Pentagon to take stake in Venezuelan oil venture: The Pentagon will reportedly a 35% stake in "North American Blue Energy Partners," run by Alejandro Betancourt, a Venezuelan businessman close to Rodriguez who authorities have investigated after allegations of money laundering. The stake will come through "penny warrants," allowing Washington to acquire shares for a token price with little upfront spending. The U.S. could also buy 20% of the company's future oil output at cost. Russian strike hits transportation infrastructure in Danube grain hub: A Russian drone strike on transport infrastructure in the Izmail district, a major Danube grain hub near Ukraine's border with Romania, five trucks loaded with grain and damaged three others Saturday. One person was killed, and three were wounded in the attack, according to Ukrainian officials. Ukraine 's former defense minister seeks U.S. money for new weapons fund: Former Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov is seeking U.S. investment for a new defense-tech fund that would both finance and create Ukrainian weapons companies, the Financial Times . Fedorov said the fund would initially focus on battlefield robots, cheap, high-speed interceptor drones, and low-cost, AI-enabled missiles, saying Ukraine needs faster weapons development if the war continues. He also offered to help the U.S. "build an army of drones" in exchange for American Patriot missile interceptors, which are in shortfall due to the U.S. war with Iran. Fedorov, fired by President Zelenskyy last month, said Ukraine is currently "gradually, slowly losing" the war and suggested: "If we don't respond to these issues, they will smash us." UN Security Council convenes emergency meeting on Haiti: The UN Security Council an emergency meeting on Sunday following a gang attack last week in Kenscoff, outside Port-au-Prince. At least 47 people were killed, including five children, more than 50 abducted, and 2,600 displaced. UN officials said some victims were executed at a church being used as a refuge and warned that gangs continue expanding beyond the capital. Council members overwhelmingly called for the rapid deployment and September renewal of the 5,500-member Gang Suppression Force, alongside tighter enforcement of the arms embargo. The U.S. said the force must "neutralize the threat," while Russia highlighted the continued flow of weapons from the United States for heavily arming Haiti's gangs. UN data has found that more than 80% of traced firearms were manufactured in or imported from the United States, with trafficking networks centered heavily in Florida. The broader humanitarian situation in Haiti is rapidly deteriorating, with 1.5 million people are internally displaced, half of them children, and more than 2.6 million children in need of aid. 1,600 schools are closed on the island, and only 10% of inpatient health facilities in Port-au-Prince remain operational. **Want to know what's really in your food? The Trump administration is trying to help** By Bobby Jindal and Taylor Hood
---
Americans have a right to know what is in their food.

That shouldn’t be controversial. You should be able to walk into a grocery store, read a label, and be confident that the ingredients listed on the food you are buying have been subject to transparent, science-based oversight and are safe for consumption. The Trump administration has now taken an important step toward doing exactly that.

The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) proposed a rule requiring food manufacturers to notify the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) whenever they determine that an added substance is Generally Recognized as Safe, or "GRAS." When Congress passed the Food Additives Amendment in 1958, the idea was simple: ingredients with a documented history of safe use or those that qualified experts had agreed were safe should not face the same pre-market approval process as brand-new food additives. Everyday substances like salt, vinegar, black pepper, and baking powder fall into this category. Unfortunately, our regulatory system has fallen short of that basic standard. And over time, the exception became the rule.

Under the current system, manufacturers can self-determine whether a new additive is GRAS and introduce it to the U.S. food supply without notifying the FDA or the public. The manufacturer is still responsible for maintaining evidence to support its own determination, but the FDA may have no advance notice when a new substance enters the supply chain.

[**Finish reading at FoxNews.com**](http://links.americanxt.com/u/click?_t=45ea7b9dcedb45198104e7ca02a78270&_m=eaf6d66fee6f495aa2f4d0572994e921&_e=StSNkRssVRzHp6c4vkXjHCQH3KfHza8mI4f5uxeH62yz_3ISBWyX8O_awl8S3-cBcww_OV3IDzQYektV7SquhKoS7-OeYF7Cd3xYburvlEXiD6u6pasEpqzSnfBzPLiPxaO9M9JG4OZkhTCckDvzt4auLndX5imc-31ccvLU-zgd1wnw4C7kSVX8foJTsubkVFiQPRBfdyMvxMsY7KobNukUl3RjLx7QC8MQVM-Pws7twU3gaM1oInSymrs4QsdnJIYZA659OQrYYjrSGANGNnsM_90fJlwiQZqo9DZsgtgn9EjbHq5C1om5wNIfd2pqwQny9cFZZA5IV9HO709E0l6Ri3FyVeq7e-lldbZ3QEE1ZIe9DMcsHeRA45WP9qv_eZpcX1lmJm43-e2ItBgA15ytP5hgupCVqerMY_OPWJKUk4LXQ1rsiAAx7TzJSrPB_Y7vn4cx6UOXtdcW4mERUVSj39rlhccJAaZgQRIVOLQ%3D)

subject: Not an exaggeration
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
#
We’re not exaggerating: most members of Congress fuel their reelection campaigns by dedicating hours of their time asking rich donors for $500, $1,000, or even $3,500 donations.
**Alexandria is different. She doesn’t do a single minute of “call time” or host swanky cocktail fundraisers.**
This whole movement is fueled by online contributions like the ones we’re asking for in this email. With these contributions, we’ve built a campaign that is...
1. Raising resources, recruiting volunteers, and making calls to elect progressive allies across Congress and help Democrats take back the House in November.
2. Hosting several community events around the year such as our back-to-school backpack giveaways and Thanksgiving turkey distributions.
3. Raising money for community relief organizations, closing critical resource gaps that the federal government has left unfilled.
4. **Working day and night to reelect AOC, defeat our Republican opponent, and show the world what we can do.**

body:
I’m the co-founder of Voto Latino, and we’re currently facing an important fundraising deadline at midnight.
#
Hi Peter, it’s María Teresa Kumar.
I’m the co-founder of Voto Latino, and we’re currently facing an important fundraising deadline at midnight.
Voto Latino is the largest and most successful grassroots organization building Latino political power — but none of our work would be possible without supporters like you who believe in this work as much as I do.
**And what we raise before midnight will determine the resources we have to register and mobilize Latino voters heading into September, where our community will be the margin of victory — or defeat in a few short weeks.** In states like Texas, Georgia, Nevada, and Pennsylvania, where control of the U.S. Senate and the House are on the line.
**But our team just told me we still need to raise $4,500 to reach our $25,000 goal.** If we don’t, we’ll have to cut back on our plans to register, inform, and turnout Latino voters in battleground races, risking handing Donald Trump another two years of unchecked power. And with less than 10 weeks left until Election Day, we won’t have time to make up the gap.
**[So, if you’re able, can you chip in a donation of any amount today? Our team is ready to put your donation to work _immediately_.](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260831-1.3j-6Hv&amount=3&refcode=em20260831-534&t=26&akid=534%2E1366028%2EPKNK9m)**

subject: Show solidarity to public media stations affected by Trump's cuts! >>

body:
Will you be an ally to Democrats fighting to defend our democracy from Trump’s attacks?

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138246022/643575009/858395174?refcode=083126_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTAwNzkiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMDI5YjdmMmUtNWNhNS1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5YThkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=hRKQHQ-SQGNdUWKM7KOESrX83dXB0ADHCfaspB7C4wA=)

Just like I stood up to my colleagues then, I’m not going to soften the truth now to make folks comfortable. Encountering racism is the reality of running to be the first Black governor of South Carolina. _But we can’t let this hate decide whether people like me get to lead. _

Meet Joe Males:

**Joe Males is a Marine Veteran, small business-owner, city council member, and most importantly, a father. Throughout his life, he has put service to his community at the forefront of his life’s mission.

Shortly after turning 18, Joe enlisted in the Marine Corps. He attended boot camp in Camp Pendleton and later served overseas in the Philippines and Guam. After being discharged as a Sergeant, Joe remained committed to supporting his fellow veterans. He took on leadership roles in his local Elks Lodge and American Legion post, working to ensure veterans in the community had the resources and support they deserved.

Following his time in the Marine Corps, Joe carried his strong work ethic and discipline into the field of computer networking services. He started in an entry-level position, worked his way through multiple leadership roles, and in 1996, he built his own business from the ground up. Joe knows firsthand the hard work and sacrifice of this journey, and he’s determined to make it easier for hardworking Americans to do the same.

Joe’s entry into politics was deeply personal. After his son, a Marine who followed in his footsteps, was tragically murdered back home, Joe vowed that no parent should have to endure such a loss. Determined to take a stand for public safety and the rule of law, he ran for Hemet City Council to help ensure no other family would experience the same tragedy.

During his tenure on the City Council, Joe has led numerous initiatives to improve infrastructure, drive business growth, and keep neighborhoods safe and clean. He takes pride in his ability to collaborate with fellow council members and get results, even when facing different perspectives. Joe is committed to bringing this same results-driven approach to Washington D.C., to ensure the voices of the American people are heard and their needs are met.

| | | I need to tell you something I don't talk about enough.

Outside of my office, a group of extremists gathered and screamed what translates to**"Death to Krishnamoorthi"** at the top of their lungs.

A crowd of people, in America, calling for my death.

I'm an immigrant. The son of people who came to this country with nothing because they believed it was a place where you could live freely, speak freely, and serve your community without fearing for your life. A place where disagreement didn't end in threats of violence.

Sadly, this is nothing new. I have faced this before.

A sitting Republican elected official also publicly tagged the Department of Homeland Security on social media to report me as a **"foreign occupier"** with an **"unpronounceable name"** and called for the mass deportation of Indians. I have been mocked, threatened, and told in a hundred different ways that someone like me doesn't belong in American public life.
